units.he: מִן־ הַבְּהֵמָה֙ הַטְּהוֹרָ֔ה וּמִן־ הַ֨בְּהֵמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֵינֶ֖נָּה טְהֹרָ֑ה וּמִ֨ן־ הָע֔וֹף וְכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־ רֹמֵ֖שׂ עַל־ הָֽאֲדָמָֽה׃
units.en: From the clean animals, from the animals that were not clean, from the birds, and from everything that moves upon the ground,
meaningNotes: This verse’s list is completed by the verb in the next verse.
displayMeaningNotes: This verse’s list is completed by the verb in the next verse.

units.he: שְׁנַ֨יִם שְׁנַ֜יִם בָּ֧אוּ אֶל־ נֹ֛חַ אֶל־ הַתֵּבָ֖ה זָכָ֣ר וּנְקֵבָ֑ה כּֽ͏ַאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶת־ נֹֽחַ׃
units.en: two by two they came to Noach, into the ark, male and female, as God had commanded Noach.

units.he: וֽ͏ַיְהִ֖י לְשִׁבְעַ֣ת הַיָּמִ֑ים וּמֵ֣י הַמַּבּ֔וּל הָי֖וּ עַל־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃
units.en: After the seven days, the floodwaters were upon the earth.

units.he: בִּשְׁנַ֨ת שֵׁשׁ־ מֵא֤וֹת שָׁנָה֙ לְחַיֵּי־ נֹ֔חַ בַּחֹ֙דֶשׁ֙ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י בְּשִׁבְעָֽה־ עָשָׂ֥ר י֖וֹם לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֗ה נִבְקְעוּ֙ כָּֽל־ מַעְיְנֹת֙ תְּה֣וֹם רַבָּ֔ה וַאֲרֻבֹּ֥ת הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם נִפְתָּֽחוּ׃
units.en: In the six-hundredth year of Noach’s life, in the second month, on the seventeenth day of the month, on that day all the springs of the great deep burst open, and the windows of the heavens were opened.

units.he: וֽ͏ַיְהִ֥י הַגֶּ֖שֶׁם עַל־ הָאָ֑רֶץ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים י֔וֹם וְאַרְבָּעִ֖ים לָֽיְלָה׃
units.en: The rain was upon the earth for forty days and forty nights.

units.he: מִן בְּעִירָא דַּכְיָא וּמִן בְּעִירָא דִּי לֵיתָהָא דַּכְיָא וּמִן עוֹפָא וְכֹל דִּי רָחֵשׁ עַל אַרְעָא:
units.en: From the clean animals, from the animals that were not clean, from the birds, and from everything that moves upon the earth,
meaningNotes: The list continues into the following verse.
displayMeaningNotes: The list continues into the following verse.

units.he: תְּרֵין תְּרֵין עַלּוּ לְוַת נֹחַ לְתֵבוֹתָא דְּכַר וְנָקְבָּא כְּמָא דִי פַקֵּיד יְיָ יָת נֹחַ:
units.en: two by two they came in to Noach, into the ark, male and female, as the LORD had commanded Noach.

units.he: וַהֲוָה לִזְמַן שִׁבְעַת יוֹמִין וּמֵי טוֹפָנָא הֲווֹ עַל אַרְעָא:
units.en: At the appointed time of seven days, the floodwaters were upon the earth.

units.he: בִּשְׁנַת שִׁתְּ מְאָה שְׁנִין לְחַיֵּי נֹחַ בְּיַרְחָא תִּנְיָנָא בְּשִׁבְעַת עַשְׂרָא יוֹמָא לְיַרְחָא בְּיוֹמָא הָדֵין אִתְבְּזָעוּ כָּל מַבּוּעֵי תְּהוֹמָא רַבָּא וְכַוֵּי שְׁמַיָּא אִתְפַּתָּחוּ:
units.en: In the six-hundredth year of Noach’s life, in the second month, on the seventeenth day of the month, on that day all the springs of the great deep burst open, and the windows of the heavens were opened.

units.he: וַהֲוָה מִטְרָא נָחַת עַל אַרְעָא אַרְבְּעִין יְמָמִין וְאַרְבְּעִין לֵילָוָן:
units.en: Rain came down upon the earth for forty days and forty nights.

units.he: בְּרֶ֥גַע קָטֹ֖ן עֲזַבְתִּ֑יךְ וּבְרַחֲמִ֥ים גְּדֹלִ֖ים אֲקַבְּצֵֽךְ׃
units.en: For a small moment I abandoned you, but with great compassion I will gather you.

units.he: בְּשֶׁ֣צֶף קֶ֗צֶף הִסְתַּ֨רְתִּי פָנַ֥י רֶ֙גַע֙ מִמֵּ֔ךְ וּבְחֶ֥סֶד עוֹלָ֖ם רִֽחַמְתִּ֑יךְ אָמַ֥ר גֹּאֲלֵ֖ךְ יְהוָֽה׃
units.en: In a surge of anger I hid My face from you for a moment, but with everlasting kindness I have had compassion on you, says your Redeemer, the LORD.

units.he: כִּי־ מֵ֥י נֹ֙חַ֙ זֹ֣את לִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִשְׁבַּ֗עְתִּי מֵעֲבֹ֥ר מֵי־ נֹ֛חַ ע֖וֹד עַל־ הָאָ֑רֶץ כֵּ֥ן נִשְׁבַּ֛עְתִּי מִקְּצֹ֥ף עָלַ֖יִךְ וּמִגְּעָר־ בָּֽךְ׃
units.en: For this is like the waters of Noach to Me: as I swore that the waters of Noach would no longer pass over the earth, so I have sworn not to be angry with you or rebuke you.

units.he: כִּ֤י הֶֽהָרִים֙ יָמ֔וּשׁוּ וְהַגְּבָע֖וֹת תְּמוּטֶ֑נָה וְחַסְדִּ֞י מֵאִתֵּ֣ךְ לֹֽא־ יָמ֗וּשׁ וּבְרִ֤ית שְׁלוֹמִי֙ לֹ֣א תָמ֔וּט אָמַ֥ר מְרַחֲמֵ֖ךְ יְהוָֽה׃
units.en: For the mountains may depart and the hills may totter, but My kindness will not depart from you, and My covenant of peace will not totter, says the LORD, who has compassion on you.

units.he: עֲנִיָּ֥ה סֹעֲרָ֖ה לֹ֣א נֻחָ֑מָה הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י מַרְבִּ֤יץ בַּפּוּךְ֙ אֲבָנַ֔יִךְ וִיסַדְתִּ֖יךְ בַּסַּפִּירִֽים׃
units.en: Afflicted one, storm-tossed and not comforted! I am setting your stones in antimony, and will lay your foundations with sapphires.
meaningNotes: Antimony is a dark mineral pigment; the building image contrasts the setting with precious stones.
displayMeaningNotes: Antimony is a dark mineral pigment; the building image contrasts the setting with precious stones.

units.he: בְּשָׁעָה זְעֵירָא רְחַקְתִּיךְ וּבְרַחֲמִין סַגִיאִין אֲקָרֵב גַלְוָתָךְ:
units.en: For a little while I kept you at a distance, but with great compassion I will bring your exiles near.

units.he: בִּרְגַז זְעֵיר סַלְקִית אַפֵי שְׁכִנְתִּי זְמַן זְעֵירָא מִנִיךְ וּבְטַבְוַת עֲלָם דְלָא פְסָקָן אֲרַחֵם עֲלָךְ אֲמַר פָּרְקִיךְ יְיָ:
units.en: In a little anger I withdrew the face of My Divine Presence from you for a little while, but with everlasting kindnesses that do not cease I will have compassion on you, says your Redeemer, the LORD.

units.he: כְּיוֹמֵי נֹחַ דָא קֳדָמַי דְקַיְמֵית בְּמֵימְרִי דְלָא יֶעְדוּן מֵי טוּפָנָא דַהֲווֹ בְּיוֹמֵי נֹחַ עוֹד עַל אַרְעָא כֵּן קַיְמִית בְּמֵימְרִי דְלָא יֵחוֹל רוּגְזִי עֲלָךְ וְלָא אֶזוֹף בִּיךְ:
units.en: This is like the days of Noach before Me: as I established by My word that the floodwaters that were in the days of Noach would no longer pass over the earth, so I have established by My word that My anger will not rest upon you and I will not rebuke you.

units.he: אֲרֵי טוּרַיָא יֶעְדוּן וְרָמָתָא יִתְפַּרְקוּן וְטוּבִי מִנִיךְ יְרוּשְׁלֵם לָא יֶעְדֵי וּקְיַם שְׁלָמִי לָא יִתְרְחַק אֲמַר דְעָתִיד לְרַחֲמָא עֲלָךְ יְיָ:
units.en: For the mountains may pass away and the hills may be broken apart, but My goodness will not pass away from you, Jerusalem, and My covenant of peace will not be removed, says the LORD, who will have compassion on you.

units.he: חֲשִׁיבָתָא מְקַבְּלָא עוּלְבַּן קַרְתָּא דְאָמְרִין עֲלָה עַמְמַיָא לָא תִתְנְחֵם הָא אֲנָא כָּבֵשׁ בִצְדִידָא אַבְנֵי רִצְפָּתִיךְ וַאֲשַׁכְלְלִינִיךְ בְּאַבְנִין טָבִין:
units.en: Afflicted [or: esteemed] one, receiving humiliation, city of which the peoples say, “She will not be comforted”! I am laying the stones of your pavement in antimony, and will complete you with precious stones.
meaningNotes: The opening חֲשִׁיבָתָא is lexically uncertain. The surrounding humiliation, and the similar wording for the poor in 58:7, support an afflicted or impoverished city; the same stem elsewhere can mean “regarded” or “esteemed.” The peoples’ statement “She will not be comforted” is not the Divine promise that follows.
displayMeaningNotes: The opening חֲשִׁיבָתָא permits an afflicted or impoverished reading in this context; elsewhere the same stem can mean “regarded” or “esteemed.” Both meanings remain possible. The peoples say “She will not be comforted”; the Divine speaker then promises to rebuild the city.

units.he: אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָרְחֹתֵיהֶ֣ם עִקְּשִׁ֑ים וּ֝נְלוֹזִ֗ים בְּמַעְגְּלוֹתָֽם׃
units.en: whose paths are crooked, and who are devious in their ways;
meaningNotes: The opening describes the evildoers in the preceding verses. Wisdom’s protection continues in the next verse.
displayMeaningNotes: The opening describes the evildoers in the preceding verses. Wisdom’s protection continues in the next verse.

units.he: לְ֭הַצִּ֣ילְךָ מֵאִשָּׁ֣ה זָרָ֑ה מִ֝נָּכְרִיָּ֗ה אֲמָרֶ֥יהָ הֶחֱלִֽיקָה׃
units.en: to rescue you from the strange woman, from the foreign woman who makes her words smooth,
meaningNotes: The “strange” or “foreign” woman is described here through her betrayal of her youthful companion and covenant; the verse is not a general statement about foreign-born women.
displayMeaningNotes: The “strange” or “foreign” woman is described here through her betrayal of her youthful companion and covenant; the verse is not a general statement about foreign-born women.

units.he: הַ֭עֹזֶבֶת אַלּ֣וּף נְעוּרֶ֑יהָ וְאֶת־ בְּרִ֖ית אֱלֹהֶ֣יהָ שָׁכֵֽחָה׃
units.en: who abandons the companion of her youth and has forgotten the covenant of her God.

units.he: כִּ֤י שָׁ֣חָה אֶל־ מָ֣וֶת בֵּיתָ֑הּ וְאֶל־ רְ֝פָאִ֗ים מַעְגְּלֹתֶֽיהָ׃
units.en: For her house sinks toward death, and her paths toward the shades of the dead.

units.he: כָּל־ בָּ֭אֶיהָ לֹ֣א יְשׁוּב֑וּן וְלֹֽא־ יַ֝שִּׂ֗יגוּ אָרְח֥וֹת חַיִּֽים׃
units.en: All who go to her do not return, and do not reach the paths of life.

units.he: דְאָרְחָתְהוֹן מְעַקְמָן וּמִפַּתְּלִין שְׁבִילֵיהוֹן:
units.en: whose ways are crooked and whose paths are twisted;

units.he: דְתִתְפְּצֵי מִן אִתְּתָא חִילוֹנִיתָא מִנוּכְרֵיתָא דְמִלָהָא חַלְיָן:
units.en: so that you will be delivered from the outsider woman, from the foreign woman whose words are sweet,

units.he: דְשָׁבְקָה מַרְבִּיתָא דְטַלְיוּתָהָא וּקְיָמָא דֶאֱלָהָא טְעָת:
units.en: who abandons the upbringing of her youth and has forgotten the covenant of God.
meaningNotes: The Targum’s מַרְבִּיתָא denotes nurture or upbringing, rather than a youthful companion.
displayMeaningNotes: The Targum’s מַרְבִּיתָא denotes nurture or upbringing, rather than a youthful companion.

units.he: דִבְעִמְקָא דְמוֹתָא בֵיתָהּ וּלְגִבָרַיָא הִלְכָתָא דִשְׁבִילָהָא:
units.en: For her house is in the depth of death, and the course of her paths leads to the mighty ones [of the dead].
meaningNotes: The Aramaic literally says “mighty ones”; the setting of death supplies the bracketed qualification.
displayMeaningNotes: The Aramaic literally says “mighty ones”; the setting of death supplies the bracketed qualification.

units.he: כָּל דְעָיְלָן לָא חָזְרִין בִּשְׁלָם וְלָא צָיְדִין אָרְחָתָא דְחַיֵי:
units.en: All who enter do not return in peace and do not attain the paths of life.

units.he: כָּל הַזְּבָחִים שֶׁקִּבֵּל דָּמָן זָר, אוֹנֵן, טְבוּל יוֹם, מְחֻסַּר בְּגָדִים, מְחֻסַּר כִּפּוּרִים, שֶׁלֹּא רְחוּץ יָדַיִם וְרַגְלַיִם, עָרֵל, טָמֵא, יוֹשֵׁב, עוֹמֵד עַל גַּבֵּי כֵלִים, עַל גַּבֵּי בְהֵמָה, עַל גַּבֵּי רַגְלֵי חֲבֵרוֹ, פָּסָל. קִבֵּל בַּשְּׂמֹאל, פָּסָל. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַכְשִׁיר. נִשְׁפַּךְ הַדָּם עַל הָרִצְפָּה וַאֲסָפוֹ, פָּסוּל. נְתָנוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי הַכֶּבֶשׁ שֶׁלֹּא כְנֶגֶד הַיְסוֹד, נָתַן אֶת הַנִּתָּנִין לְמַטָּן, לְמַעְלָן, וְאֶת הַנִּתָּנִין לְמַעְלָן, לְמַטָּן, אֶת הַנִּתָּנִים בִּפְנִים, בַּחוּץ, וְאֶת הַנִּתָּנִין בַּחוּץ, בִּפְנִים, פָּסוּל וְאֵין בּוֹ כָרֵת:
units.en: All sacrifices whose blood was received by a non-priest, one in acute mourning, one who immersed that day, a priest lacking the required garments, one awaiting the offerings that complete purification, one who had not washed hands and feet, an uncircumcised person, an impure person, one sitting, or one standing on vessels, on an animal, or on his fellow’s feet, were invalidated. If he received with the left hand, he invalidated it; Rabbi Shimon declares it valid. If the blood spilled onto the floor and he gathered it up, it is invalid. If he put it on the ramp, not opposite the base; put above what should be applied below, or below what should be applied above; put outside what should be applied inside, or inside what should be applied outside—it is invalid, but there is no liability for excision.
meaningNotes: Excision is the penalty category for eating certain disqualified sacrificial food; its absence does not erase other possible liability. Acute mourning here includes the day a close relative dies; it is not limited to the time before burial, and the High Priest has a distinct exception. The floor-spill case concerns blood not first received in a service vessel.
displayMeaningNotes: Excision is the penalty category for eating certain disqualified sacrificial food; its absence does not erase other possible liability. Acute mourning here includes the day a close relative dies; it is not limited to the time before burial, and the High Priest has a distinct exception. The floor-spill case concerns blood not first received in a service vessel.

units.he: הַשּׁוֹחֵט אֶת הַזֶּבַח לִזְרֹק דָּמוֹ בַחוּץ אוֹ מִקְצָת דָּמוֹ בַחוּץ, לְהַקְטִיר אֶת אֵמוּרָיו בַּחוּץ אוֹ מִקְצָת אֵמוּרָיו בַּחוּץ, לֶאֱכֹל בְּשָׂרוֹ בַחוּץ אוֹ כַזַּיִת מִבְּשָׂרוֹ בַחוּץ אוֹ לֶאֱכֹל כַּזַּיִת מֵעוֹר הָאַלְיָה בַחוּץ, פָּסוּל וְאֵין בּוֹ כָרֵת. לִזְרֹק דָּמוֹ לְמָחָר אוֹ מִקְצָת דָּמוֹ לְמָחָר, לְהַקְטִיר אֵמוּרָיו לְמָחָר אוֹ מִקְצָת אֵמוּרָיו לְמָחָר, לֶאֱכֹל בְּשָׂרוֹ לְמָחָר אוֹ כַזַּיִת מִבְּשָׂרוֹ לְמָחָר אוֹ כַּזַּיִת מֵעוֹר הָאַלְיָה לְמָחָר, פִּגּוּל וְחַיָּבִין עָלָיו כָּרֵת:
units.en: One who slaughters a sacrifice intending to apply its blood outside, or some of its blood outside; to burn its altar portions outside, or some of its altar portions outside; to eat its flesh outside, or an olive-sized amount of its flesh outside, or an olive-sized amount of the skin of the fat-tail outside: it is invalid, but there is no liability for excision. [If he intends] to apply its blood tomorrow, or some of its blood tomorrow; to burn its altar portions tomorrow, or some of its altar portions tomorrow; to eat its flesh tomorrow, or an olive-sized amount of its flesh tomorrow, or an olive-sized amount of the skin of the fat-tail tomorrow: it is disqualified by an improper-time intention, and eating it incurs liability for excision.
meaningNotes: “Outside” means outside the offering’s assigned place. “Tomorrow” is an improper-time intention only when it exceeds the permitted time for that offering or service; eating peace-offering flesh tomorrow is not automatically an improper-time case. Improper intentions are distinct from performing the acts themselves. The improper-time penalty also requires completion of the permitting service without another invalidating defect, as explained in 2:3–4.
displayMeaningNotes: “Outside” means outside the offering’s assigned place. “Tomorrow” is an improper-time intention only when it exceeds the permitted time for that offering or service; eating peace-offering flesh tomorrow is not automatically an improper-time case. Improper intentions are distinct from performing the acts themselves. The improper-time penalty also requires completion of the permitting service without another invalidating defect, as explained in 2:3–4.

units.he: זֶה הַכְּלָל, כָּל הַשּׁוֹחֵט וְהַמְקַבֵּל וְהַמְהַלֵּךְ וְהַזּוֹרֵק, לֶאֱכֹל דָּבָר שֶׁדַּרְכּוֹ לֶאֱכֹל, לְהַקְטִיר דָּבָר שֶׁדַּרְכּוֹ לְהַקְטִיר, חוּץ לִמְקוֹמוֹ, פָּסוּל וְאֵין בּוֹ כָרֵת. חוּץ לִזְמַנּוֹ, פִּגּוּל וְחַיָּבִין עָלָיו כָּרֵת, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיִּקְרַב הַמַּתִּיר כְּמִצְוָתוֹ:
units.en: This is the rule: Anyone who slaughters, receives, carries, or applies the blood, intending to eat something ordinarily eaten or burn something ordinarily burned outside its proper place, makes it invalid, but without liability for excision. Outside its proper time, it is disqualified by an improper-time intention, and eating it incurs liability for excision—provided that the permitting service is offered in its prescribed manner.
meaningNotes: The permitting service is the blood service that permits the offering’s later consumption or altar use. Its required qualification is explained by the alternative cases in the next Mishna.
displayMeaningNotes: The permitting service is the blood service that permits the offering’s later consumption or altar use. Its required qualification is explained by the alternative cases in the next Mishna.

units.he: כֵּיצַד קָרַב הַמַּתִּיר כְּמִצְוָתוֹ. שָׁחַט בִּשְׁתִיקָה, קִבֵּל וְהִלֵּךְ וְזָרַק חוּץ לִזְמַנּוֹ. אוֹ שֶׁשָּׁחַט חוּץ לִזְמַנּוֹ, קִבֵּל וְהִלֵּךְ וְזָרַק בִּשְׁתִיקָה. אוֹ שֶׁשָּׁחַט, וְקִבֵּל וְהִלֵּךְ וְזָרַק חוּץ לִזְמַנּוֹ, זֶה הוּא שֶׁקָּרַב הַמַּתִּיר כְּמִצְוָתוֹ. כֵּיצַד לֹא קָרַב הַמַּתִּיר כְּמִצְוָתוֹ. שָׁחַט חוּץ לִמְקוֹמוֹ, קִבֵּל וְהִלֵּךְ וְזָרַק חוּץ לִזְמַנּוֹ. אוֹ שֶׁשָּׁחַט חוּץ לִזְמַנּוֹ, קִבֵּל וְהִלֵּךְ וְזָרַק חוּץ לִמְקוֹמוֹ. אוֹ שֶׁשָּׁחַט, קִבֵּל, וְהִלֵּךְ, וְזָרַק, חוּץ לִמְקוֹמוֹ. הַפֶּסַח וְהַחַטָּאת שֶׁשְּׁחָטָן שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָן, קִבֵּל וְהִלֵּךְ וְזָרַק חוּץ לִזְמַנּוֹ. אוֹ שֶׁשָּׁחַט חוּץ לִזְמַנּוֹ, קִבֵּל וְהִלֵּךְ וְזָרַק שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָן. אוֹ שֶּׁשָּׁחַט, קִבֵּל, וְהִלֵּךְ, וְזָרַק, שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָן. זֶה הוּא שֶׁלֹּא קָרַב הַמַּתִּיר כְּמִצְוָתוֹ:
units.en: How was the permitting service offered in its prescribed manner? He slaughtered without a disqualifying intention, and received, carried, and applied [the blood] with an improper-time intention; or slaughtered with an improper-time intention, and received, carried, and applied without a disqualifying intention; or slaughtered, received, carried, and applied with an improper-time intention. This is a case in which the permitting service was offered in its prescribed manner. How was the permitting service not offered in its prescribed manner? He slaughtered with an improper-place intention, and received, carried, and applied with an improper-time intention; or slaughtered with an improper-time intention, and received, carried, and applied with an improper-place intention; or slaughtered, received, carried, and applied with an improper-place intention. [Likewise,] a Passover offering or sin offering that he slaughtered not for its own designation, and received, carried, and applied with an improper-time intention; or slaughtered with an improper-time intention, and received, carried, and applied not for its own designation; or slaughtered, received, carried, and applied not for its own designation. This is a case in which the permitting service was not offered in its prescribed manner.
meaningNotes: “In its prescribed manner” here means without a separate invalidating defect besides improper-time intention; it does not make that intention valid. Each “or” introduces an alternative, not a chronological continuation.
displayMeaningNotes: “In its prescribed manner” here means without a separate invalidating defect besides improper-time intention; it does not make that intention valid. Each “or” introduces an alternative, not a chronological continuation.

units.he: לֶאֱכֹל כַּזַּיִת בַּחוּץ וְכַזַּיִת לְמָחָר, כַּזַּיִת לְמָחָר וְכַזַּיִת בַּחוּץ, כַּחֲצִי זַיִת בַּחוּץ וְכַחֲצִי זַיִת לְמָחָר, כַּחֲצִי זַיִת לְמָחָר וְכַחֲצִי זַיִת בַּחוּץ, פָּסוּל וְאֵין בּוֹ כָרֵת. אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, זֶה הַכְּלָל, אִם מַחֲשֶׁבֶת הַזְּמָן קָדְמָה לְמַחֲשֶׁבֶת הַמָּקוֹם, פִּגּוּל וְחַיָּבִים עָלָיו כָּרֵת. וְאִם מַחֲשֶׁבֶת הַמָּקוֹם קָדְמָה לְמַחֲשֶׁבֶת הַזְּמָן, פָּסוּל וְאֵין בּוֹ כָרֵת. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים זֶה וָזֶה פָסוּל וְאֵין בּוֹ כָרֵת. לֶאֱכֹל כַּחֲצִי זַיִת וּלְהַקְטִיר כַּחֲצִי זַיִת, כָּשֵׁר, שֶׁאֵין אֲכִילָה וְהַקְטָרָה מִצְטָרְפִין:
units.en: [If he intends] to eat an olive-sized amount outside and an olive-sized amount tomorrow; an olive-sized amount tomorrow and an olive-sized amount outside; half an olive-sized amount outside and half an olive-sized amount tomorrow; or half an olive-sized amount tomorrow and half an olive-sized amount outside—it is invalid, but there is no liability for excision. Rabbi Yehudah said: This is the rule: If the improper-time intention preceded the improper-place intention, it is disqualified by an improper-time intention, and eating it incurs liability for excision. If the improper-place intention preceded the improper-time intention, it is invalid, but without liability for excision. The Sages say: In either case it is invalid, but without liability for excision. [If he intends] to eat half an olive-sized amount and burn half an olive-sized amount, it is valid, because eating and burning do not combine.

units.he: מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי, אֵין מוֹכְרִין אוֹתוֹ, וְאֵין מְמַשְׁכְּנִין אוֹתוֹ, וְאֵין מַחֲלִיפִין אוֹתוֹ, וְלֹא שׁוֹקְלִין כְּנֶּגְדּוֹ. וְלֹא יֹאמַר אָדָם לַחֲבֵרוֹ בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם, הֵילָךְ יַיִן וְתֶן לִי שָׁמֶן. וְכֵן שְׁאָר כָּל הַפֵּרוֹת. אֲבָל נוֹתְנִין זֶה לָזֶה מַתְּנַת חִנָּם:
units.en: Second-tithe produce may not be sold, pledged, exchanged, or used as a counterweight. A person in Jerusalem may not say to his friend, “Here is wine; give me oil,” and the same applies to all other produce. But they may give one another outright gifts.

units.he: מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה, אֵין מוֹכְרִין אוֹתוֹ תָּמִים חַי, וְלֹא בַעַל מוּם חַי וְשָׁחוּט, וְאֵין מְקַדְּשִׁין בּוֹ הָאִשָּׁה. הַבְּכוֹר מוֹכְרִין אוֹתוֹ תָּמִים חַי, וּבַעַל מוּם חַי וְשָׁחוּט, וּמְקַדְּשִׁין בּוֹ הָאִשָּׁה. אֵין מְחַלְּלִין מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי עַל אֲסִימוֹן, וְלֹא עַל הַמַּטְבֵּעַ שֶׁאֵינוֹ יוֹצֵא, וְלֹא עַל הַמָּעוֹת שֶׁאֵינָן בִּרְשׁוּתוֹ:
units.en: An animal-tithe offering may not be sold unblemished and alive, nor blemished, whether alive or slaughtered; a woman may not be betrothed with it. A firstborn animal may be sold unblemished and alive, or blemished, whether alive or slaughtered; a woman may be betrothed with it. Second tithe may not be redeemed onto an unstamped coin, a coin that is not current, or money that is not in one’s possession.

units.he: הַלּוֹקֵחַ בְּהֵמָה לְזִבְחֵי שְׁלָמִים, אוֹ חַיָּה לִבְשַׂר תַּאֲוָה, יָצָא הָעוֹר לְחֻלִּין, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהָעוֹר מְרֻבֶּה עַל הַבָּשָׂר. כַּדֵּי יַיִן סְתוּמוֹת, מְקוֹם שֶׁדַּרְכָּן לִמְכֹּר סְתוּמוֹת, יָצָא קַנְקַן לְחֻלִּין. הָאֱגוֹזִים וְהַשְּׁקֵדִים, יָצְאוּ קְלִפֵּיהֶם לְחֻלִּין. הַתֶּמֶד, עַד שֶׁלֹּא הֶחְמִיץ, אֵינוֹ נִלְקָח בְּכֶסֶף מַעֲשֵׂר. וּמִשֶּׁהֶחְמִיץ, נִלְקָח בְּכֶסֶף מַעֲשֵׂר:
units.en: If one buys a domestic animal for peace offerings, or a wild animal for ordinary meat, the hide becomes ordinary property, even if the hide is worth more than the meat. With sealed jars of wine, in a place where they are ordinarily sold sealed, the jar becomes ordinary property. With walnuts and almonds, their shells become ordinary property. Grape-pomace drink before it has fermented may not be bought with tithe money; once it has fermented, it may be bought with tithe money.
meaningNotes: “Ordinary property” means that tithe sanctity is not retained by the incidental hide, jar, or shells in these cases.
displayMeaningNotes: “Ordinary property” means that tithe sanctity is not retained by the incidental hide, jar, or shells in these cases.

units.he: הַלּוֹקֵחַ חַיָּה לְזִבְחֵי שְׁלָמִים, בְּהֵמָה לִבְשַׂר תַּאֲוָה, לֹא יָצָא הָעוֹר לְחֻלִּין. כַּדֵּי יַיִן פְּתוּחוֹת אוֹ סְתוּמוֹת, מְקוֹם שֶׁדַּרְכָּן לִמָּכֵר פְּתוּחוֹת, לֹא יָצָא קַנְקַן לְחֻלִּין. סַלֵּי זֵיתִים וְסַלֵּי עֲנָבִים עִם הַכְּלִי, לֹא יָצְאוּ דְמֵי הַכְּלִי לְחֻלִּין:
units.en: If one buys a wild animal for peace offerings, or a domestic animal for ordinary meat, the hide does not become ordinary property. With open or sealed wine jars, in a place where they are ordinarily sold open, the jar does not become ordinary property. With baskets of olives or baskets of grapes together with the container, the container’s price does not become ordinary property.
meaningNotes: The wild animal cannot be a peace offering; the reversed purchase purposes are distinct from the permitted cases above.
displayMeaningNotes: The wild animal cannot be a peace offering; the reversed purchase purposes are distinct from the permitted cases above.

units.he: הַלּוֹקֵחַ מַיִם, וּמֶלַח, וּפֵרוֹת הַמְחֻבָּרִים לַקַּרְקַע, אוֹ פֵרוֹת שֶׁאֵינָן יְכוֹלִין לְהַגִּיעַ לִירוּשָׁלַיִם, לֹא קָנָה מַעֲשֵׂר. הַלּוֹקֵחַ פֵּרוֹת, שׁוֹגֵג, יַחְזְרוּ דָמִים לִמְקוֹמָן. מֵזִיד, יָעֳלוּ וְיֵאָכְלוּ בַמָּקוֹם. וְאִם אֵין מִקְדָּשׁ, יֵרַקְּבוּ:
units.en: If one buys water, salt, produce attached to the ground, or produce that cannot reach Jerusalem, the purchase has not acquired the status of second tithe. If one buys produce unintentionally [in a prohibited purchase], the money must be returned to where it came from; intentionally, the produce must be brought up and eaten in the place [Jerusalem]. If there is no Sanctuary, it must be left to rot.
meaningNotes: “The place” is Jerusalem. Unintentional purchase, intentional purchase, and absence of the Sanctuary are separate legal branches. The unintentional case requires return of the purchase money, not merely reclassification of it.
displayMeaningNotes: “The place” is Jerusalem. Unintentional purchase, intentional purchase, and absence of the Sanctuary are separate legal branches. The unintentional case requires return of the purchase money, not merely reclassification of it.

units.he: הַלּוֹקֵחַ בְּהֵמָה, שׁוֹגֵג, יַחְזְרוּ דָמֶיהָ לִמְקוֹמָן. מֵזִיד, תָּעֳלֶה וְתֵאָכֵל בַּמָּקוֹם. וְאִם אֵין מִקְדָּשׁ, תִּקָּבֵר עַל יְדֵי עוֹרָהּ:
units.en: If one buys a domestic animal unintentionally [in a prohibited purchase], its price must be returned to where it came from; intentionally, the animal must be brought up and eaten in the place [Jerusalem]. If there is no Sanctuary, it must be buried with its hide.

units.he: אֵין לוֹקְחִין עֲבָדִים וּשְׁפָחוֹת וְקַרְקָעוֹת וּבְהֵמָה טְמֵאָה מִדְּמֵי מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי. וְאִם לָקַח, יֹאכַל כְּנֶגְדָּן. אֵין מְבִיאִין קִנֵּי זָבִים, וְקִנֵּי זָבוֹת, וְקִנֵּי יוֹלְדוֹת, חַטָּאוֹת, וַאֲשָׁמוֹת, מִדְּמֵי מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי. וְאִם הֵבִיא, יֹאכַל כְּנֶגְדָּם. זֶה הַכְּלָל, כָּל שֶׁהוּא חוּץ לַאֲכִילָה וְלִשְׁתִיָּה וּלְסִיכָה מִדְּמֵי מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי, יֹאכַל כְּנֶגְדּוֹ:
units.en: One may not buy male slaves, female slaves, land, or an unclean animal with second-tithe money. If one bought them, he must eat [permitted food] equal to their value. One may not bring the bird-pairs of men or women with discharges, the bird-pairs of women after childbirth, sin offerings, or guilt offerings from second-tithe money. If one brought them, he must eat [permitted food] equal to their value. This is the rule: For any expenditure of second-tithe money outside eating, drinking, or anointing, he must eat [permitted food] equal to its value.
meaningNotes: The equal-value consumption is a compensating tithe obligation, not consumption of the purchased slaves, land, or offerings.
displayMeaningNotes: The equal-value consumption is a compensating tithe obligation, not consumption of the purchased slaves, land, or offerings.

units.he: וְשֶׁלֹּא רָחוּץ יָדַיִם וְרַגְלַיִם. אָתְיָא ״חוּקָּה״–״חוּקָּה״ מִמְּחוּסַּר בְּגָדִים.
units.en: ‘And one who has not washed his hands and feet’: This is derived by the verbal analogy of ‘statute’ with ‘statute’ from one lacking the priestly garments.

units.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל שֶׁלֹּא טָבַל וְשֶׁלֹּא קִידֵּשׁ בֵּין בֶּגֶד לְבֶגֶד וּבֵין עֲבוֹדָה לַעֲבוֹדָה, וְעָבַד – עֲבוֹדָתוֹ כְּשֵׁרָה. וְאֶחָד כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל וְאֶחָד כֹּהֵן הֶדְיוֹט שֶׁלֹּא קִידֵּשׁ יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו שַׁחֲרִית, וְעָבַד – עֲבוֹדָתוֹ פְּסוּלָה.
units.en: The Rabbis taught: If a high priest did not immerse and did not sanctify his hands and feet between one set of garments and another, or between one service and another, but performed the service, his service is valid. But whether a high priest or an ordinary priest, if he did not sanctify his hands and feet in the morning and performed the service, his service is invalid.

units.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַסִּי לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מִכְּדִי חָמֵשׁ טְבִילוֹת וַעֲשָׂרָה קִדּוּשִׁין דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא, וְ״חוּקָּה״ כְּתִיב בְּהוּ – לִיעַכְּבוּ!
units.en: Rav Asi said to Rabbi Yohanan: Since the five immersions and ten sanctifications are required by Torah law, and ‘statute’ is written concerning them, let their omission invalidate the service!

units.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, אָמַר קְרָא: ״וּלְבֵשָׁם״ – לְבִישָׁה מְעַכֶּבֶת, וְאֵין דָּבָר אַחֵר מְעַכֵּב.
units.en: He said to him: Scripture says, ‘And put them on’: Dressing is indispensable, but no other matter [in that verse] is indispensable.

units.he: צָהֲבוּ פָּנָיו, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וָי״ו אַאוּפְתָּא כְּתַבִי לָךְ – אִי הָכִי, דְּצַפְרָא נָמֵי.
units.en: His face brightened. He said to him: I have written a vav on a block of wood for you [an explanation that does not stand up to scrutiny]: If so, the morning sanctification should not be indispensable either.

units.he: אָמַר חִזְקִיָּה, אָמַר קְרָא: ״וְהָיְתָה לָהֶם חׇק עוֹלָם לוֹ וּלְזַרְעוֹ לְדֹרֹתָם״ – דָּבָר הַמְעַכֵּב בְּזַרְעוֹ, מְעַכֵּב בּוֹ; דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְעַכֵּב בְּזַרְעוֹ, אֵין מְעַכֵּב בּוֹ.
units.en: Hizkiyah said: Scripture says, ‘It shall be an everlasting statute for them, for him and his descendants throughout their generations’: A requirement indispensable for his descendants is indispensable for him; one not indispensable for his descendants is not indispensable for him.

units.he: רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן אָמַר מֵהָכָא: ״וְרָחֲצוּ מִמֶּנּוּ מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו״ – דָּבָר הַמְעַכֵּב בְּבָנָיו מְעַכֵּב בּוֹ, דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְעַכֵּב בְּבָנָיו אֵין מְעַכֵּב בּוֹ.
units.en: Rabbi Yonatan said that it is derived from here: ‘Moses, Aaron, and his sons washed from it’: A requirement indispensable for his sons is indispensable for him; one not indispensable for his sons is not indispensable for him.

units.he: רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר מִדְּחִזְקִיָּה? אָמַר לָךְ: הָהוּא לְדוֹרוֹת הוּא דִּכְתִיב.
units.en: Why did Rabbi Yonatan not use Hizkiyah’s verse? He could say to you: That verse is written concerning future generations.

units.he: וְאִידַּךְ – מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר מֵהַאי? מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא – דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: כׇּל כִּיּוֹר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ כְּדֵי לְקַדֵּשׁ אַרְבָּעָה כֹּהֲנִים מִמֶּנּוּ – אֵין מְקַדְּשִׁין בּוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְרָחֲצוּ מִמֶּנּוּ מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו״.
units.en: And why did the other sage not use this verse? He needs it for Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Hanina’s teaching. Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Hanina said: Any laver that does not contain enough water for four priests to sanctify themselves from it may not be used for sanctification, as it is said, ‘Moses, Aaron, and his sons washed from it.’

units.he: כהן גדול כגון בחמש עבודות של יוה״כ שהוא משנה מבגדי זהב לבגדי לבן ומבגדי לבן לבגדי זהב וצריך לכל חילוף טבילה ושני קידושין מן המקרא:
units.en: ‘A high priest’: For example, in the five services on the Day of Atonement, when he changes from gold garments to white garments and from white garments to gold garments. For each change, Scripture requires an immersion and two sanctifications [of his hands and feet].

units.he: שחרית בין ביוה״כ בין בכל השנה עבודתו פסולה כדילפינן חוקה חוקה ממחוסר בגדים:
units.en: ‘In the morning’: Whether on the Day of Atonement or during the rest of the year, his service is invalid, as we derive through the verbal analogy of ‘statute’ with ‘statute’ from one lacking the priestly garments.

units.he: דאורייתא דכתיב ורחץ את בשרו במים ולבשם:
units.en: ‘Required by Torah law’: For it is written, ‘He shall wash his flesh in water and put them on.’

units.he: וחוקה כתיב בהו לאחר שגמר כל הפרשה כתיב והיתה לכם לחוקת עולם וגו׳:
units.en: ‘And “statute” is written concerning them’: After completing the whole passage, Scripture says, ‘It shall be an everlasting statute for you,’ and so on.

units.he: ולבשם שנה הכתוב בלבישה לעכב דכתיב ילבש ולבשם ולהכי כתיב הכא עכובא למעוטי עכובא דחוקה דלא קיימא אהאי קרא דאיירי ברחיצה ולבישה אלא אשאר דברים האמורים בפרשה:
units.en: ‘And put them on’: Scripture repeats the dressing requirement to make it indispensable, writing both ‘he shall wear’ and ‘put them on.’ It makes this requirement indispensable here to exclude the indispensability implied by ‘statute’: that word does not apply to this verse, which concerns washing and dressing, but to the other matters in the passage.

units.he: ואין דבר אחר בפסוק זה מעכב:
units.en: ‘And no other matter’: No other matter in this verse is indispensable.

units.he: צהבו פניו של רבי אסי מפני שמחה כסבור טעם הגון שמע:
units.en: ‘His face brightened’: Rabbi Asi’s face brightened with joy; he thought he had heard a sound explanation.

units.he: ויו אאופתא כלומר דאיכא לאקשויי א״כ אפי׳ קידוש של שחרית של יוה״כ נמי לא לעכב ביה דהא אימעוט ביוה״כ מולבשם:
units.en: ‘A vav on a block of wood’: Meaning that one can object: If so, even the morning sanctification on the Day of Atonement should not be indispensable, because it too was excluded on the Day of Atonement by ‘put them on.’

units.he: והיתה להם חק עולם בקידוש כתיב:
units.en: ‘It shall be an everlasting statute for them’: This is written concerning sanctification [of hands and feet].

units.he: דבר המעכב בזרעו בכהנים הדיוטים דהיינו קידוש שבשעת כניסה שנוהג בכל הכהנים מעכבא באהרן ביוה״כ דהא חוקה כתיב:
units.en: ‘A requirement indispensable for his descendants’: For ordinary priests—namely, the sanctification upon entering, which applies to all priests—is also indispensable for Aaron on the Day of Atonement, because ‘statute’ is written.

units.he: לדורות הוא דכתיב אזהרה לנהוג חוקה זו לזרעו אחריו ולא להיקשא אתא:
units.en: ‘It is written for the generations’: It is an injunction that his descendants after him observe this statute, not a textual comparison.

units.he: שאין בו שאין מחזיק מים כשיעור ארבעה קידושין:
units.en: ‘Which does not contain’: It does not hold enough water for four sanctifications.

units.he: משה ואהרן תרין ובניו תרין שאף משה כהן היה בשבעת ימי המילואים:
units.en: ‘Moses and Aaron’: Two; ‘and his sons’: Two. Moses, too, was a priest during the seven days of inauguration.

units.he: צריך אדם להתרחק מהנשים מאד מאד ואסור לקרוץ בידיו או ברגליו ולרמוז בעיניו לאחת מהעריות ואסור לשחוק עמה להקל ראשו כנגדה או להביט ביופיה:
units.en: A man must keep very far from women. It is forbidden to gesture with his hands or feet, or signal with his eyes, to one of the women forbidden to him; it is forbidden to joke with her, behave frivolously toward her, or gaze at her beauty.
displayMeaningNotes: This daily excerpt is not the complete legal subsection or all Rema glosses, and is not a personal practical ruling.

units.he: אין שואלים בשלום אשה כלל:
units.en: One must not inquire after a woman’s well-being at all.
displayMeaningNotes: This daily excerpt is not the complete legal subsection or all Rema glosses, and is not a personal practical ruling. Even HaEzer 21:6 includes a permitted inquiry to her husband about her well-being. That alternative is omitted from this short compiler clause; “at all” must not be presented as a complete inventory of permitted and forbidden inquiries.

units.he: המחבק ומנשק אחת מהעריות שאין לבו נוקפו כגון אחותו הגדולה ואחות אביו הרי זה מגונה ודבר איסור הוא ומעשה טפשים שאין קריבה לערוה כלל חוץ מהאב לבתו והאם לבנה:
units.en: One who embraces or kisses a forbidden relative toward whom his heart feels no temptation, such as his grown sister or his father’s sister, acts reprehensibly: it is forbidden and foolish conduct. There is to be no physical closeness to a forbidden relative at all, except for a father with his daughter and a mother with her son.
displayMeaningNotes: This daily excerpt is not the complete legal subsection or all Rema glosses, and is not a personal practical ruling. The 1874 daily reading gives the father’s sister as its example. The full subsection includes further kinship and age qualifications.

units.he: אסור להתייחד עם ערוה מהעריות בין זקנה בין ילדה שדבר זה גורם לגלות ערוה חוץ מהאם עם בנה והאב עם בתו:
units.en: It is forbidden to be secluded with a woman forbidden to him, whether old or young, because this leads to forbidden relations, except for a mother with her son and a father with his daughter.
displayMeaningNotes: This daily excerpt is not the complete legal subsection or all Rema glosses, and is not a personal practical ruling. The complete subsection contains other conditions and exceptions beyond these two kinship examples.

units.he: דוד ובית דינו גזרו על יחוד פנויה ואפי׳ שאינה ערוה:
units.en: David and his court decreed against seclusion with an unmarried woman, even when she is not otherwise a forbidden relation.
displayMeaningNotes: This daily excerpt is not the complete legal subsection or all Rema glosses, and is not a personal practical ruling. This is the compilation’s David/court clause, not the complete historical account or every later branch of22:2.

units.he: כל המתייחד עם אשה שאסור להתייחד עמה בין ישראלית בין גויה מכין שניהם מכת מרדות ומכריזין עליהם חוץ מאשת איש:
units.en: Anyone who is secluded with a woman with whom seclusion is forbidden, whether a Jewish woman or a non-Jewish woman, is punished together with her by disciplinary lashes, and their conduct is publicly announced—except in the case of a married woman.
displayMeaningNotes: This daily excerpt is not the complete legal subsection or all Rema glosses, and is not a personal practical ruling. The source reports historical court-administered corporal discipline and public proclamation; it does not authorize private punishment, coercion, or public shaming. Its married-woman exception is abbreviated. Even HaEzer 22:2 gives the rationale about avoiding allegations against her and her children; do not turn this shortened clause into a contemporary enforcement instruction.

units.he:
"ומוראכם וחתכם יהיה" -- מכאן ולהלאה יהא לכון דיוקנין דבני נשא, דהא בקדמיתא לא הוו דיוקנין דבני נשא, תא חזי בקדמיתא כתיב (שם ט ו) בצלם אלהי"ם עשה את האדם, וכתיב (שם ה א) בדמות אלהי"ם עשה אותו, כיון דחטו אשתנו דיוקנייהו מההוא דיוקנא עלאה, ואתהפכו אינון למדחל מקמי חיוון ברא, בקדמיתא כל בריין דעלמא זקפן עיינין וחמאן דיוקנא קדישא עלאה, וזעאן ודחלין מקמיה, כיון דחטו אתהפך דיוקניהו מעינייהו לדיוקנא אחרא, ואתהפך דבני נשא זעין ודחלין מקמי שאר בריין. 

תא חזי כל אינון בני נשא דלא חטאן קמי מאריהון ולא עברין על פקודי אורייתא, זיו דיוקנא דלהון לא אשתני מחיזו דדיוקנא עלאה, וכל בריין דעלמא זעין ודחלין קמיה, ובשעתא דבני נשא עברין על פתגמי אורייתא, אתחלף דיוקנא דלהון, וכלהו זעין ודחלין מקמי בריין אחרנין, בגין דאתחלף דיוקנא עלאה, ואתעבר מנייהו, וכדין שלטי בהו חיות ברא, דהא לא חמו בהו ההוא דיוקנא עלאה כדקחזי. ועל כן השתא כיון דעלמא אתחדש כמלקדמין, בריך לון ברכתא דא, ושליט לון על כלא, כמה דאת אמר ובכל דגי הים בידכם נתנו, ואפילו נוני ימא, רבי חייא אמר, בידכם נתנו מקדמת דנא, דכד ברא קב"ה עלמא, מסר כלא בידהון, דכתיב ורדו בדגת הים ובעוף השמים וגו'.
units.en:
“Your fear and your dread shall be”—from now on you shall have the forms of human beings, for previously they did not have the forms of human beings. Come and see: at the beginning it is written, “In the image of God He made the human being” (ibid., 9:6), and it is written, “In the likeness of God He made him” (ibid., 5:1). When they sinned, their forms changed from that supernal form, and they were changed so as to fear the beasts of the field. At the beginning all the creatures of the world raised their eyes, saw the holy supernal form, and trembled and feared before it. When they sinned, their form changed in [the creatures’] eyes to another form, and it came about that human beings trembled and feared before the other creatures.

Come and see: all those people who do not sin before their Master and do not transgress the commandments of the Torah—the radiance of their form does not change from the appearance of the supernal form, and all the creatures of the world tremble and fear before it. But when people transgress the words of the Torah, their form changes, and they all tremble and fear before other creatures, because the supernal form has changed and has departed from them. Then the beasts of the field rule over them, for they do not see that supernal form in them as they should. Therefore now, since the world has been renewed as at first, He blessed them with this blessing and gave them dominion over everything, as it says, “And all the fish of the sea—into your hand they have been given”; even the fish of the sea. Rabbi Chiya said: “Into your hand they have been given” was so before this, for when the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world, He entrusted everything into their hands, as it is written, “Rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the heavens,” etc.
displayMeaningNotes: The supernal human form before sin and the changed form after sin are contrasted. The claims about animals’ fear and human dominion are mystical teachings, not zoological observations. The bracketed possessive concerns the creatures’ eyes; the following fear belongs to human beings.
Rabbi Chiya says that dominion, including over the fish of the sea, was given already at creation.

units.he:
כל הנאות וטובות העולם הזה הבל המה מעשה תעתועים. ולמה תתגאה על הבריות, אם בקומה זקופה, כולם נבראו בצלם אלהים כמוך. ואם במשפחה, כולנו בני איש אחד נחנו בני אברהם יצחק ויעקב. ואם בעושר, כמה ריקים ופוחזים ממך, עשירים יותר ממך. ועוד כי ה' מוריש ומעשיר ואל יתהלל עשיר בעשרו כי באולי עושר שמור לבעליו לרעתו. ואם בשררה וכבוד, כמה בזויי משפחה שולטים בעולם, כמו שכתוב (משלי ל כב): "תחת עבד כי ימלוך". ועוד כי העושר והכבוד מלפניו והוא משפיל גאים עדי ארץ. ואם בחכמה, כמה חכמים גדולים נטרדו מהעולם הזה ומהעולם הבא, כענין דואג ואחיתופל וירבעם, ובידו יתברך להסיר שפה לנאמנים וטעם זקנים יקח, ואל יתהלל חכם בחכמתו, ואיך תתגאה ותחלתך נולדת מטפה סרוחה ובמעבר השתן נכנסת ויצאת, בושה וכלימה אתה בחייך רמה ותולעה במותך ואף כי עפר אתה ואל עפר תשוב והיה כלא היה:
ואיך תכעוס על זולתך ולא תכעוס עליך שאתה בעצמך טורף נפשך באפך ועובד עבודה זרה בכעסך, ואתה מכעיס את קונך ועתיד ליפרע ממך, ואיך תקפיד על הבלי העולם הזה וסופך למות ורוח עברה בו ואיננו ולא יכירנו עוד מקומו רואיו יאמרו איו, ואיך תתעצב על עולם שאינו שלך ולא תתעצב על פרידת נפשך מגופך ברתת וזיע ואימה חשיכה נופלת עליו, ואיך תחמוד לצבור זהב ולבנות בתים ועליות מרווחים, והוא לקברות יובל אמה על אמה ברום אמה בארץ תחתיה ומאומה אין בידך ועזבת לאחרים חילד, ולמה תיגע להעשיר והכל תלוי במזל אפילו ספר תורה שבהיכל
units.en:
All the pleasures and good things of this world are vanity, a work of delusions. Why should you exalt yourself above other people? If it is because of an upright stature, all were created in the image of God, like you. If it is because of family, we are all the sons of one man, sons of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. If it is because of wealth, how many people emptier and more reckless than you are wealthier than you! Moreover, ה' impoverishes and enriches, and a rich person should not glory in his wealth, for perhaps wealth is kept for its owner's harm. If it is because of authority and honour, how many people of despised family rule in the world, as it is written (Mishlay 30:22): ‘Under a servant when he becomes king.’ Moreover, wealth and honour come from Him, and He brings the proud down to the earth. If it is because of wisdom, how many great sages were driven out of this world and the World to Come, such as Doeg, Ahithophel, and Jeroboam! It is in His hand, blessed is He, to remove speech from the trustworthy and to take the discernment of elders; a wise person should not glory in his wisdom. How can you be proud, when at your beginning you were born from a putrid drop, and through the passage of urine you entered and emerged? You are shame and humiliation in your lifetime, maggots and worms at your death; moreover, you are dust and to dust you will return, and he will be as though he had not been.

How can you be angry with someone else and not be angry with yourself, when you yourself tear your soul in your anger and worship idolatry in your wrath? You anger your Creator, Who will exact payment from you. How can you take offence over the vanities of this world when your end is to die? ‘A wind passes over him and he is no more, and his place knows him no longer’; those who saw him will say, ‘Where is he?’ How can you grieve over a world that is not yours, and not grieve over your soul's separation from your body amid trembling and quaking, with a dark dread falling upon him? How can you covet the hoarding of gold and the building of houses and spacious upper rooms, when he will be brought to graves—a cubit by a cubit, a cubit high, in the earth below—with nothing in your hand? You will leave [your wealth] to others. Why toil to become rich? Everything depends on fortune, even a Torah scroll in the sanctuary.

meaningNotes.he: ״חילד״ מופיע כאן בהקשר של צבירת זהב והנחת רכוש לאחרים, ומובנו נקרא ״[רכושך]״. בלשון המקבילה בחק נאמר ״חילך״; ״חילד״ היא לשון הקטע כאן.
meaningNotes.en: חילד occurs here in the context of hoarding gold and leaving property to others, and is read as “[your wealth]”. The parallel Chok wording is חילך; חילד is the wording of this passage.

meaningNotes.he: מידות הקבר הן חלק מן התוכחה על קטנות המקום לעומת הבתים המרווחים, ולא הוראה מעשית למידות קבר. הקטע עובר מלשון נוכח ללשון נסתר ב״והוא לקברות יובל״ ובלשון האימה הנופלת ״עליו״.
meaningNotes.en: The burial dimensions belong to the rebuke contrasting a small burial place with spacious houses, not a practical ruling about grave dimensions. The passage shifts from addressing ‘you’ to speaking of ‘him’ in ‘he will be brought to graves’ and in the dread falling ‘upon him.’

meaningNotes.he: ״מזל״ מתאר כאן גורל או הצלחה שאינם מובטחים על ידי המאמץ, עד שאפילו ספר תורה שבהיכל עשוי לזכות למעמד שונה. האמירה חותמת את הקריאה היומית; אין זו הוראה לבטל השתדלות או לעסוק באסטרולוגיה. האמירה על כעס ועבודה זרה היא לשון התוכחה החריפה של המחבר.
meaningNotes.en: ‘Fortune’ here describes the allotment or success that effort cannot guarantee, so that even a Torah scroll in the sanctuary may receive a different standing. This statement closes the daily reading; it is not an instruction to abandon effort or practise astrology. The statement associating anger with idolatry belongs to the author's forceful language of rebuke.

displayMeaningNotes.he: ״חילד״ מופיע כאן בהקשר של צבירת זהב והנחת רכוש לאחרים, ומובנו נקרא ״[רכושך]״. בלשון המקבילה בחק נאמר ״חילך״; ״חילד״ היא לשון הקטע כאן.
displayMeaningNotes.en: חילד occurs here in the context of hoarding gold and leaving property to others, and is read as “[your wealth]”. The parallel Chok wording is חילך; חילד is the wording of this passage.

displayMeaningNotes.he: מידות הקבר הן חלק מן התוכחה על קטנות המקום לעומת הבתים המרווחים, ולא הוראה מעשית למידות קבר. הקטע עובר מלשון נוכח ללשון נסתר ב״והוא לקברות יובל״ ובלשון האימה הנופלת ״עליו״.

The passage shifts from addressing ‘you’ to speaking of ‘him’ in ‘he will be brought to graves’ and in the dread falling ‘upon him.’

displayMeaningNotes.he: ״מזל״ מתאר כאן גורל או הצלחה שאינם מובטחים על ידי המאמץ, עד שאפילו ספר תורה שבהיכל עשוי לזכות למעמד שונה. האמירה חותמת את הקריאה היומית; אין זו הוראה לבטל השתדלות או לעסוק באסטרולוגיה. האמירה על כעס ועבודה זרה היא לשון התוכחה החריפה של המחבר.
displayMeaningNotes.en: ‘Fortune’ here describes the allotment or success that effort cannot guarantee, so that even a Torah scroll in the sanctuary may receive a different standing. This statement closes the daily reading; it is not an instruction to abandon effort or practise astrology. The statement associating anger with idolatry belongs to the author's forceful language of rebuke.

finalSelectedPair.title: Vanity, pride, anger, and mortality
finalSelectedPair.original:
כל הנאות וטובות העולם הזה הבל המה מעשה תעתועים. ולמה תתגאה על הבריות, אם בקומה זקופה, כולם נבראו בצלם אלהים כמוך. ואם במשפחה, כולנו בני איש אחד נחנו בני אברהם יצחק ויעקב. ואם בעושר, כמה ריקים ופוחזים ממך, עשירים יותר ממך. ועוד כי ה' מוריש ומעשיר ואל יתהלל עשיר בעשרו כי באולי עושר שמור לבעליו לרעתו. ואם בשררה וכבוד, כמה בזויי משפחה שולטים בעולם, כמו שכתוב (משלי ל כב): "תחת עבד כי ימלוך". ועוד כי העושר והכבוד מלפניו והוא משפיל גאים עדי ארץ. ואם בחכמה, כמה חכמים גדולים נטרדו מהעולם הזה ומהעולם הבא, כענין דואג ואחיתופל וירבעם, ובידו יתברך להסיר שפה לנאמנים וטעם זקנים יקח, ואל יתהלל חכם בחכמתו, ואיך תתגאה ותחלתך נולדת מטפה סרוחה ובמעבר השתן נכנסת ויצאת, בושה וכלימה אתה בחייך רמה ותולעה במותך ואף כי עפר אתה ואל עפר תשוב והיה כלא היה:
ואיך תכעוס על זולתך ולא תכעוס עליך שאתה בעצמך טורף נפשך באפך ועובד עבודה זרה בכעסך, ואתה מכעיס את קונך ועתיד ליפרע ממך, ואיך תקפיד על הבלי העולם הזה וסופך למות ורוח עברה בו ואיננו ולא יכירנו עוד מקומו רואיו יאמרו איו, ואיך תתעצב על עולם שאינו שלך ולא תתעצב על פרידת נפשך מגופך ברתת וזיע ואימה חשיכה נופלת עליו, ואיך תחמוד לצבור זהב ולבנות בתים ועליות מרווחים, והוא לקברות יובל אמה על אמה ברום אמה בארץ תחתיה ומאומה אין בידך ועזבת לאחרים חילד, ולמה תיגע להעשיר והכל תלוי במזל אפילו ספר תורה שבהיכל
finalSelectedPair.english:
All the pleasures and good things of this world are vanity, a work of delusions. Why should you exalt yourself above other people? If it is because of an upright stature, all were created in the image of God, like you. If it is because of family, we are all the sons of one man, sons of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. If it is because of wealth, how many people emptier and more reckless than you are wealthier than you! Moreover, ה' impoverishes and enriches, and a rich person should not glory in his wealth, for perhaps wealth is kept for its owner's harm. If it is because of authority and honour, how many people of despised family rule in the world, as it is written (Mishlay 30:22): ‘Under a servant when he becomes king.’ Moreover, wealth and honour come from Him, and He brings the proud down to the earth. If it is because of wisdom, how many great sages were driven out of this world and the World to Come, such as Doeg, Ahithophel, and Jeroboam! It is in His hand, blessed is He, to remove speech from the trustworthy and to take the discernment of elders; a wise person should not glory in his wisdom. How can you be proud, when at your beginning you were born from a putrid drop, and through the passage of urine you entered and emerged? You are shame and humiliation in your lifetime, maggots and worms at your death; moreover, you are dust and to dust you will return, and he will be as though he had not been.

How can you be angry with someone else and not be angry with yourself, when you yourself tear your soul in your anger and worship idolatry in your wrath? You anger your Creator, Who will exact payment from you. How can you take offence over the vanities of this world when your end is to die? ‘A wind passes over him and he is no more, and his place knows him no longer’; those who saw him will say, ‘Where is he?’ How can you grieve over a world that is not yours, and not grieve over your soul's separation from your body amid trembling and quaking, with a dark dread falling upon him? How can you covet the hoarding of gold and the building of houses and spacious upper rooms, when he will be brought to graves—a cubit by a cubit, a cubit high, in the earth below—with nothing in your hand? You will leave [your wealth] to others. Why toil to become rich? Everything depends on fortune, even a Torah scroll in the sanctuary.

units.he: בְּעֶ֨צֶם הַיּ֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ בָּ֣א נֹ֔חַ וְשֵׁם־ וְחָ֥ם וָיֶ֖פֶת בְּנֵי־ נֹ֑חַ וְאֵ֣שֶׁת נֹ֗חַ וּשְׁלֹ֧שֶׁת נְשֵֽׁי־ בָנָ֛יו אִתָּ֖ם אֶל־ הַתֵּבָֽה׃
units.en: On that very day, Noach entered the ark, together with Shem, Cham, and Yefes, Noach’s sons, Noach’s wife, and the three wives of his sons with them.

units.he: הֵ֜מָּה וְכָל־ הֽ͏ַחַיָּ֣ה לְמִינָ֗הּ וְכָל־ הַבְּהֵמָה֙ לְמִינָ֔הּ וְכָל־ הָרֶ֛מֶשׂ הָרֹמֵ֥שׂ עַל־ הָאָ֖רֶץ לְמִינֵ֑הוּ וְכָל־ הָע֣וֹף לְמִינֵ֔הוּ כֹּ֖ל צִפּ֥וֹר כָּל־ כָּנָֽף׃
units.en: They, and every wild animal according to its kind, every domestic animal according to its kind, every moving creature that moves upon the earth according to its kind, and every flying creature according to its kind—every bird, every winged creature—
meaningNotes: The list in this verse is completed by “came” in the following verse.
displayMeaningNotes: The list in this verse is completed by “came” in the following verse.

units.he: וַיָּבֹ֥אוּ אֶל־ נֹ֖חַ אֶל־ הַתֵּבָ֑ה שְׁנַ֤יִם שְׁנַ֙יִם֙ מִכָּל־ הַבָּשָׂ֔ר אֲשֶׁר־ בּ֖וֹ ר֥וּחַ חַיִּֽים׃
units.en: came to Noach into the ark, two by two, from all flesh in which there was the breath of life.

units.he: וְהַבָּאִ֗ים זָכָ֨ר וּנְקֵבָ֤ה מִכָּל־ בָּשָׂר֙ בָּ֔אוּ כּֽ͏ַאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה אֹת֖וֹ אֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיִּסְגֹּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה בּֽ͏ַעֲדֽוֹ׃
units.en: Those entering came male and female from all flesh, as God had commanded him; and the LORD shut him in.

units.he: וֽ͏ַיְהִ֧י הַמַּבּ֛וּל אַרְבָּעִ֥ים י֖וֹם עַל־ הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיִּרְבּ֣וּ הַמַּ֗יִם וַיִּשְׂאוּ֙ אֶת־ הַתֵּבָ֔ה וַתָּ֖רָם מֵעַ֥ל הָאָֽרֶץ׃
units.en: The flood was upon the earth for forty days. The waters increased and lifted the ark, and it rose above the earth.

units.he: וַיִּגְבְּר֥וּ הַמַּ֛יִם וַיִּרְבּ֥וּ מְאֹ֖ד עַל־ הָאָ֑רֶץ וַתֵּ֥לֶךְ הַתֵּבָ֖ה עַל־ פְּנֵ֥י הַמָּֽיִם׃
units.en: The waters grew strong and increased greatly upon the earth, and the ark moved upon the surface of the waters.

units.he: וְהַמַּ֗יִם גָּֽבְר֛וּ מְאֹ֥ד מְאֹ֖ד עַל־ הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיְכֻסּ֗וּ כָּל־ הֽ͏ֶהָרִים֙ הַגְּבֹהִ֔ים אֲשֶׁר־ תַּ֖חַת כָּל־ הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃
units.en: The waters grew exceedingly strong upon the earth, and all the high mountains beneath all the heavens were covered.

units.he: חֲמֵ֨שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה אַמָּה֙ מִלְמַ֔עְלָה גָּבְר֖וּ הַמָּ֑יִם וַיְכֻסּ֖וּ הֶהָרִֽים׃
units.en: The waters rose fifteen cubits above, and the mountains were covered.

units.he: וַיִּגְוַ֞ע כָּל־ בָּשָׂ֣ר ׀ הָרֹמֵ֣שׂ עַל־ הָאָ֗רֶץ בָּע֤וֹף וּבַבְּהֵמָה֙ וּבַ֣חַיָּ֔ה וּבְכָל־ הַשֶּׁ֖רֶץ הַשֹּׁרֵ֣ץ עַל־ הָאָ֑רֶץ וְכֹ֖ל הָאָדָֽם׃
units.en: All flesh that moved upon the earth perished: birds, domestic animals, wild animals, every swarming creature that swarms upon the earth, and all human beings.

units.he: כֹּ֡ל אֲשֶׁר֩ נִשְׁמַת־ ר֨וּחַ חַיִּ֜ים בְּאַפָּ֗יו מִכֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר בֶּחָֽרָבָ֖ה מֵֽתוּ׃
units.en: Everything on dry land in whose nostrils was the breath of the spirit of life died.

units.he: וַיִּ֜מַח אֶֽת־ כָּל־ הַיְק֣וּם ׀ אֲשֶׁ֣ר ׀ עַל־ פְּנֵ֣י הֽ͏ָאֲדָמָ֗ה מֵאָדָ֤ם עַד־ בְּהֵמָה֙ עַד־ רֶ֙מֶשׂ֙ וְעַד־ ע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַיִּמָּח֖וּ מִן־ הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיִשָּׁ֧אֶר אַךְ־ נֹ֛חַ וֽ͏ַאֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ בַּתֵּבָֽה׃
units.en: He wiped away every living thing on the face of the ground, from human beings to domestic animals, moving creatures, and birds of the heavens. They were wiped away from the earth; only Noach and those with him in the ark remained.
meaningNotes: “He” is the source’s unstated subject, understood in context as God; the source does not repeat a Divine Name here.
displayMeaningNotes: “He” is the source’s unstated subject, understood in context as God; the source does not repeat a Divine Name here.

units.he: וַיִּגְבְּר֥וּ הַמַּ֖יִם עַל־ הָאָ֑רֶץ חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים וּמְאַ֖ת יֽוֹם׃
units.en: The waters prevailed upon the earth for one hundred and fifty days.

units.he: וַיִּזְכֹּ֤ר אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת־ נֹ֔חַ וְאֵ֤ת כָּל־ הֽ͏ַחַיָּה֙ וְאֶת־ כָּל־ הַבְּהֵמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ בַּתֵּבָ֑ה וַיַּעֲבֵ֨ר אֱלֹהִ֥ים ר֙וּחַ֙ עַל־ הָאָ֔רֶץ וַיָּשֹׁ֖כּוּ הַמָּֽיִם׃
units.en: God remembered Noach, and all the wild animals and all the domestic animals that were with him in the ark. God caused a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters subsided.

units.he: וַיִּסָּֽכְרוּ֙ מַעְיְנֹ֣ת תְּה֔וֹם וֽ͏ַאֲרֻבֹּ֖ת הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וַיִּכָּלֵ֥א הַגֶּ֖שֶׁם מִן־ הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃
units.en: The springs of the deep and the windows of the heavens were stopped up, and the rain from the heavens was restrained.

units.he: וַיָּשֻׁ֧בוּ הַמַּ֛יִם מֵעַ֥ל הָאָ֖רֶץ הָל֣וֹךְ וָשׁ֑וֹב וַיַּחְסְר֣וּ הַמַּ֔יִם מִקְצֵ֕ה חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים וּמְאַ֖ת יֽוֹם׃
units.en: The waters kept receding from the earth, and the waters diminished at the end of one hundred and fifty days.

units.he: וַתָּ֤נַח הַתֵּבָה֙ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י בְּשִׁבְעָה־ עָשָׂ֥ר י֖וֹם לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ עַ֖ל הָרֵ֥י אֲרָרָֽט׃
units.en: The ark came to rest in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, upon the mountains of Ararat.

units.he: וְהַמַּ֗יִם הָיוּ֙ הָל֣וֹךְ וְחָס֔וֹר עַ֖ד הַחֹ֣דֶשׁ הֽ͏ָעֲשִׂירִ֑י בּֽ͏ָעֲשִׂירִי֙ בְּאֶחָ֣ד לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ נִרְא֖וּ רָאשֵׁ֥י הֽ͏ֶהָרִֽים׃
units.en: The waters kept diminishing until the tenth month; in the tenth month, on the first day of the month, the tops of the mountains appeared.

units.he: וֽ͏ַיְהִ֕י מִקֵּ֖ץ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים י֑וֹם וַיִּפְתַּ֣ח נֹ֔חַ אֶת־ חַלּ֥וֹן הַתֵּבָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָֽׂה׃
units.en: At the end of forty days, Noach opened the window of the ark that he had made.
meaningNotes: The verse does not itself name the event from which these forty days are counted.
displayMeaningNotes: The verse does not itself name the event from which these forty days are counted.

units.he: וַיְשַׁלַּ֖ח אֶת־ הֽ͏ָעֹרֵ֑ב וַיֵּצֵ֤א יָצוֹא֙ וָשׁ֔וֹב עַד־ יְבֹ֥שֶׁת הַמַּ֖יִם מֵעַ֥ל הָאָֽרֶץ׃
units.en: He sent out the raven, and it went out, going to and fro, until the waters dried from the earth.

units.he: וַיְשַׁלַּ֥ח אֶת־ הַיּוֹנָ֖ה מֵאִתּ֑וֹ לִרְאוֹת֙ הֲקַ֣לּוּ הַמַּ֔יִם מֵעַ֖ל פְּנֵ֥י הֽ͏ָאֲדָמָֽה׃
units.en: He sent the dove away from him to see whether the waters had abated from the face of the ground.

units.he: וְלֹֽא־ מָצְאָה֩ הַיּוֹנָ֨ה מָנ֜וֹחַ לְכַף־ רַגְלָ֗הּ וַתָּ֤שָׁב אֵלָיו֙ אֶל־ הַתֵּבָ֔ה כִּי־ מַ֖יִם עַל־ פְּנֵ֣י כָל־ הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יָדוֹ֙ וַיִּקָּחֶ֔הָ וַיָּבֵ֥א אֹתָ֛הּ אֵלָ֖יו אֶל־ הַתֵּבָֽה׃
units.en: The dove found no resting place for the sole of its foot and returned to him into the ark, because water was over the face of all the earth. He stretched out his hand, took it, and brought it to himself into the ark.

units.he: וַיָּ֣חֶל ע֔וֹד שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים אֲחֵרִ֑ים וַיֹּ֛סֶף שַׁלַּ֥ח אֶת־ הַיּוֹנָ֖ה מִן־ הַתֵּבָֽה׃
units.en: He waited another seven days, and again sent the dove out of the ark.

units.he: וַתָּבֹ֨א אֵלָ֤יו הַיּוֹנָה֙ לְעֵ֣ת עֶ֔רֶב וְהִנֵּ֥ה עֲלֵה־ זַ֖יִת טָרָ֣ף בְּפִ֑יהָ וַיֵּ֣דַע נֹ֔חַ כִּי־ קַ֥לּוּ הַמַּ֖יִם מֵעַ֥ל הָאָֽרֶץ׃
units.en: The dove came to him toward evening, and there was a freshly plucked olive leaf in its mouth. Noach knew that the waters had abated from the earth.

units.he: וַיִּיָּ֣חֶל ע֔וֹד שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים אֲחֵרִ֑ים וַיְשַׁלַּח֙ אֶת־ הַיּוֹנָ֔ה וְלֹֽא־ יָסְפָ֥ה שׁוּב־ אֵלָ֖יו עֽוֹד׃
units.en: He waited another seven days and sent out the dove; it did not return to him again.

units.he: וֽ͏ַ֠יְהִי בְּאַחַ֨ת וְשֵׁשׁ־ מֵא֜וֹת שָׁנָ֗ה בּֽ͏ָרִאשׁוֹן֙ בְּאֶחָ֣ד לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ חָֽרְב֥וּ הַמַּ֖יִם מֵעַ֣ל הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיָּ֤סַר נֹ֙חַ֙ אֶת־ מִכְסֵ֣ה הַתֵּבָ֔ה וַיַּ֕רְא וְהִנֵּ֥ה חֽ͏ָרְב֖וּ פְּנֵ֥י הֽ͏ָאֲדָמָֽה׃
units.en: In the six-hundred-and-first year, in the first month, on the first day of the month, the waters had dried from the earth. Noach removed the covering of the ark and looked: the surface of the ground had dried.
meaningNotes: The year continues the chronology of Noach’s life; the text distinguishes the drying of the surface here from the dry earth of the following verse.
displayMeaningNotes: The year continues the chronology of Noach’s life; the text distinguishes the drying of the surface here from the dry earth of the following verse.

units.he: וּבַחֹ֙דֶשׁ֙ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י בְּשִׁבְעָ֧ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֛ים י֖וֹם לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ יָבְשָׁ֖ה הָאָֽרֶץ׃
units.en: In the second month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, the earth was dry.

units.he: בִּכְרַן יוֹמָא הָדֵין עָל נֹחַ וְשֵׁם וְחָם וָיֶפֶת בְּנֵי נֹחַ וְאִתַּת נֹחַ וּתְלָתָא נְשֵׁי בְנוֹהִי עִמְּהוֹן לְתֵבוֹתָא:
אִנּוּן וְכָל חַיְתָא לִזְנַהּ וְכָל בְּעִירָא לִזְנַהּ וְכָל רִחֲשָׁא דְּרָחֵשׁ עַל אַרְעָא לִזְנוֹהִי וְכָל עוֹפָא לִזְנוֹהִי כֹּל צִפַּר כָּל דְּפָרָח:
וְעַלּוּ עִם נֹחַ לְתֵבוֹתָא תְּרֵין תְּרֵין מִכָּל בִּשְׂרָא דִי בֵיהּ רוּחָא דְחַיֵי:
וְעָלַיָּא דְּכַר וְנָקְבָּא מִכָּל בִּשְׂרָא עַלּוּ כְּמָא דִי פַקֵּיד יָתֵיהּ יְיָ וַאֲגֵן יְיָ (בְּמֵימְרֵיהּ) עֲלוֹהִי:
וַהֲוָה טוֹפָנָא אַרְבְּעִין יוֹמִין עַל אַרְעָא וּסְגִיאוּ מַיָּא וּנְטָלוּ יָת תֵּבוֹתָא וְאִתָּרָמַת מֵעַל אַרְעָא:
וּתְקִיפוּ מַיָּא וּסְגִיאוּ לַחֲדָא עַל אַרְעָא וּמְהַלְּכָא תֵבוֹתָא עַל אַפֵּי מַיָּא:
וּמַיָּא תְּקִיפוּ לַחֲדָא לַחֲדָא עַל אַרְעָא וְאִתְחֲפִיאוּ כָּל טוּרַיָּא רָמַיָּא דִּי תְחוֹת כָּל שְׁמַיָּא:
חֲמֵשׁ עַשְׂרֵה אַמִּין מִלְעֵלָּא תְּקִיפוּ מַיָּא וְאִתְחֲפִיאוּ טוּרַיָא:
וּמִית כָּל בִּשְׂרָא דְּרָחֵשׁ עַל אַרְעָא בְּעוֹפָא וּבִבְעִירָא וּבְחַיְתָא וּבְכָל רִחֲשָׁא דְּרָחֵשׁ עַל אַרְעָא וְכֹל אֱנָשָׁא:
כֹּל דִּי נִשְׁמְתָא רוּחָא דְּחַיִּין בְּאַנְפוֹהִי מִכֹּל דִּי בְּיַבֶּשְׁתָּא מִיתוּ:
וּמְחָא יָת כָּל יְקוּמָא דִּי עַל אַפֵּי אַרְעָא מֵאֱנָשָׁא עַד בְּעִירָא עַד רִחֲשָׁא וְעַד עוֹפָא דִשְׁמַיָּא וְאִתְמְחִיאוּ מִן אַרְעָא וְאִשְׁתָּאַר בְּרַם נֹחַ וְדִי עִמֵּיהּ בְּתֵבוֹתָא:
וּתְקִיפוּ מַיָּא עַל אַרְעָא מְאָה וְחַמְשִׁין יוֹמִין:
וּדְכִיר יְיָ יָת נֹחַ וְיָת כָּל חַיְתָא וְיָת כָּל בְּעִירָא דִּי עִמֵּיהּ בְּתֵבוֹתָא וְאַעְבַּר יְיָ רוּחָא עַל אַרְעָא וְנָחוּ מַיָּא:
וְאִסְתְּכָרוּ מַבּוּעֵי תְהוֹמָא וְכַוֵּי שְׁמַיָּא וְאִתְכְּלִי מִטְרָא מִן שְׁמַיָּא:
וְתָבוּ מַיָּא מֵעַל אַרְעָא אָזְלִין וְתָיְבִין וַחֲסָרוּ מַיָּא מִסּוֹף מְאָה וְחַמְשִׁין יוֹמִין:
וְנָחַת תֵּבוֹתָא בְּיַרְחָא שְׁבִיעָאָה בְּשִׁבְעַת עֲשַׂר יוֹמָא לְיַרְחָא עַל טוּרֵי קַרְדּוּ:
וּמַיָּא הֲווֹ אָזְלִין וְחָסְרִין עַד יַרְחָא עֲשִׂירָאָה בַּעֲשִׂירָאָה בְּחַד לְיַרְחָא אִתְחֲזִיאוּ רֵישֵׁי טוּרַיָּא:
וַהֲוָה מִסּוֹף אַרְבְּעִין יוֹמִין וּפְתַח נֹחַ יָת כַּוַּת תֵּבוֹתָא דִּי עֲבָד:
וְשַׁלַּח יָת עָרְבָּא וּנְפַק מִפַּק וְתַיִב עַד דְּיַבִּישׁוּ מַיָּא מֵעַל אַרְעָא:
וְשַׁלַּח יָת יוֹנָה מִלְּוָתֵיהּ לְמֶחֱזֵי הֲקַלִּיאוּ מַיָּא מֵעַל אַפֵּי אַרְעָא:
וְלָא אַשְׁכַּחַת יוֹנָה מְנַח לְפַרְסַת רַגְלַהּ וְתָבַת לְוָתֵיהּ לְתֵבוֹתָא אֲרֵי מַיָּא עַל אַפֵּי כָל אַרְעָא וְאוֹשִׁיט יְדֵיהּ וְנָסְבַהּ וְאָעֵיל יָתַהּ לְוָתֵיהּ לְתֵבוֹתָא:
וְאוֹרִיךְ עוֹד שַׁבְעָא יוֹמִין אָחֳרָנִין וְאוֹסֵיף שַׁלַּח יָת יוֹנָה מִן תֵּבוֹתָא:
וַאֲתַת לְוָתֵיהּ יוֹנָה לְעִדַּן רַמְשָׁא וְהָא טְרַף זֵיתָא תְּבִיר נָחִית בְּפוּמַהּ וִידַע נֹחַ אֲרֵי קַלִּיאוּ מַיָא מֵעַל אַרְעָא:
וְאוֹרִיךְ עוֹד שַׁבְעָה יוֹמִין אָחֳרָנִין וְשַׁלַּח יָת יוֹנָה וְלָא אוֹסֵיפַת לְמִתּוּב לְוָתֵיהּ עוֹד:
וַהֲוָה בְּשִׁתְּ מְאָה וְחַד שְׁנִין בְּקַדְמָאָה בְּחַד לְיַרְחָא נְגוּבוּ מַיָּא מֵעַל אַרְעָא וְאַעְדִּי נֹחַ יָת חוֹפָאָה דְּתֵבוֹתָא וַחֲזָא וְהָא נְגוּבוּ אַפֵּי אַרְעָא:
וּבְיַרְחָא תִּנְיָנָא בְּעַשְׂרִין וְשַׁבְעָא יוֹמָא לְיַרְחָא יַבִּישַׁת אַרְעָא:
וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶל־ נֹ֥חַ לֵאמֹֽר׃
units.en: God spoke to Noach, saying:

units.he: צֵ֖א מִן־ הַתֵּבָ֑ה אַתָּ֕ה וְאִשְׁתְּךָ֛ וּבָנֶ֥יךָ וּנְשֵֽׁי־ בָנֶ֖יךָ אִתָּֽךְ׃
units.en: “Leave the ark—you, your wife, your sons, and your sons’ wives with you.

units.he: כָּל־ הַחַיָּ֨ה אֲשֶֽׁר־ אִתְּךָ֜ מִכָּל־ בָּשָׂ֗ר בָּע֧וֹף וּבַבְּהֵמָ֛ה וּבְכָל־ הָרֶ֛מֶשׂ הָרֹמֵ֥שׂ עַל־ הָאָ֖רֶץ הַיְצֵ֣א אִתָּ֑ךְ וְשֽׁ͏ָרְצ֣וּ בָאָ֔רֶץ וּפָר֥וּ וְרָב֖וּ עַל־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃
units.en: Bring out with you every living creature that is with you, from all flesh: birds, domestic animals, and every moving creature that moves upon the earth. Let them swarm upon the earth, be fruitful, and multiply upon the earth.”

units.he: וַיֵּ֖צֵא־ נֹ֑חַ וּבָנָ֛יו וְאִשְׁתּ֥וֹ וּנְשֵֽׁי־ בָנָ֖יו אִתּֽוֹ׃
units.en: Noach went out, together with his sons, his wife, and his sons’ wives.

units.he: כָּל־ הֽ͏ַחַיָּ֗ה כָּל־ הָרֶ֙מֶשׂ֙ וְכָל־ הָע֔וֹף כֹּ֖ל רוֹמֵ֣שׂ עַל־ הָאָ֑רֶץ לְמִשְׁפְּחֹ֣תֵיהֶ֔ם יָצְא֖וּ מִן־ הַתֵּבָֽה׃
units.en: Every wild animal, every moving creature, every bird—everything that moves upon the earth—went out from the ark according to their families.

units.he: וַיִּ֥בֶן נֹ֛חַ מִזְבֵּ֖חַ לֽ͏ַיהוָ֑ה וַיִּקַּ֞ח מִכֹּ֣ל ׀ הַבְּהֵמָ֣ה הַטְּהוֹרָ֗ה וּמִכֹּל֙ הָע֣וֹף הַטָּהֹ֔ר וַיַּ֥עַל עֹלֹ֖ת בַּמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃
units.en: Noach built an altar to the LORD. He took from every clean domestic animal and every clean bird, and offered burnt offerings on the altar.

units.he: וַיָּ֣רַח יְהוָה֮ אֶת־ רֵ֣יחַ הַנִּיחֹחַ֒ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־ לִבּ֗וֹ לֹֽא־ אֹ֠סִף לְקַלֵּ֨ל ע֤וֹד אֶת־ הָֽאֲדָמָה֙ בַּעֲב֣וּר הֽ͏ָאָדָ֔ם כִּ֠י יֵ֣צֶר לֵ֧ב הָאָדָ֛ם רַ֖ע מִנְּעֻרָ֑יו וְלֹֽא־ אֹסִ֥ף ע֛וֹד לְהַכּ֥וֹת אֶת־ כָּל־ חַ֖י כּֽ͏ַאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִֽׂיתִי׃
units.en: The LORD smelled the pleasing aroma, and the LORD said in His heart: “I will not again curse the ground because of humanity, for the inclination of the human heart is evil from youth. Nor will I again strike down every living thing as I have done.

units.he: עֹ֖ד כָּל־ יְמֵ֣י הָאָ֑רֶץ זֶ֡רַע וְ֠קָצִיר וְקֹ֨ר וָחֹ֜ם וְקַ֧יִץ וָחֹ֛רֶף וְי֥וֹם וָלַ֖יְלָה לֹ֥א יִשְׁבֹּֽתוּ׃
units.en: For all the remaining days of the earth, sowing and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night, will not cease.”

units.he: וַיְבָ֣רֶךְ אֱלֹהִ֔ים אֶת־ נֹ֖חַ וְאֶת־ בָּנָ֑יו וַיֹּ֧אמֶר לָהֶ֛ם פְּר֥וּ וּרְב֖וּ וּמִלְא֥וּ אֶת־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃
units.en: God blessed Noach and his sons and said to them: “Be fruitful, multiply, and fill the earth.

units.he: וּמוֹרַאֲכֶ֤ם וְחִתְּכֶם֙ יִֽהְיֶ֔ה עַ֚ל כָּל־ חַיַּ֣ת הָאָ֔רֶץ וְעַ֖ל כָּל־ ע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם בְּכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר תִּרְמֹ֧שׂ הֽ͏ָאֲדָמָ֛ה וּֽבְכָל־ דְּגֵ֥י הַיָּ֖ם בְּיֶדְכֶ֥ם נִתָּֽנוּ׃
units.en: The fear and dread of you will be upon every wild animal of the earth and every bird of the heavens, upon everything with which the ground teems and all the fish of the sea; they are given into your hands.

units.he: כָּל־ רֶ֙מֶשׂ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הוּא־ חַ֔י לָכֶ֥ם יִהְיֶ֖ה לְאָכְלָ֑ה כְּיֶ֣רֶק עֵ֔שֶׂב נָתַ֥תִּי לָכֶ֖ם אֶת־ כֹּֽל׃
units.en: Every moving creature that is alive shall be food for you; as with green plants, I have given you everything.

units.he: אַךְ־ בָּשָׂ֕ר בְּנַפְשׁ֥וֹ דָמ֖וֹ לֹ֥א תֹאכֵֽלוּ׃
units.en: But flesh with its life—its blood—you shall not eat.
meaningNotes: The terse phrase identifies blood with the flesh’s life. It is translated as a source statement, not a practical dietary ruling.
displayMeaningNotes: The terse phrase identifies blood with the flesh’s life. This is a source statement, not a practical dietary ruling.

units.he: וְאַ֨ךְ אֶת־ דִּמְכֶ֤ם לְנַפְשֹֽׁתֵיכֶם֙ אֶדְרֹ֔שׁ מִיַּ֥ד כָּל־ חַיָּ֖ה אֶדְרְשֶׁ֑נּוּ וּמִיַּ֣ד הֽ͏ָאָדָ֗ם מִיַּד֙ אִ֣ישׁ אָחִ֔יו אֶדְרֹ֖שׁ אֶת־ נֶ֥פֶשׁ הֽ͏ָאָדָֽם׃
units.en: And I will require an accounting for your blood, for your lives. From every animal I will require it; and from humankind, from each person for his fellow, I will require an accounting for human life.

units.he: שֹׁפֵךְ֙ דַּ֣ם הֽ͏ָאָדָ֔ם בּֽ͏ָאָדָ֖ם דָּמ֣וֹ יִשָּׁפֵ֑ךְ כִּ֚י בְּצֶ֣לֶם אֱלֹהִ֔ים עָשָׂ֖ה אֶת־ הָאָדָֽם׃
units.en: Whoever sheds human blood, by a human shall his blood be shed, for in the image of God He made humanity.
meaningNotes: The verse states a judicial principle, not permission for private violence.
displayMeaningNotes: The verse states a judicial principle, not permission for private violence.

units.he: וְאַתֶּ֖ם פְּר֣וּ וּרְב֑וּ שִׁרְצ֥וּ בָאָ֖רֶץ וּרְבוּ־ בָֽהּ׃
units.en: As for you, be fruitful and multiply; swarm upon the earth and multiply in it.”

units.he: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶל־ נֹ֔חַ וְאֶל־ בָּנָ֥יו אִתּ֖וֹ לֵאמֹֽר׃
units.en: God spoke to Noach and to his sons with him, saying:

units.he: וַאֲנִ֕י הִנְנִ֥י מֵקִ֛ים אֶת־ בְּרִיתִ֖י אִתְּכֶ֑ם וְאֶֽת־ זַרְעֲכֶ֖ם אֽ͏ַחֲרֵיכֶֽם׃
units.en: “As for Me, I am establishing My covenant with you and with your offspring after you,

units.he: וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־ נֶ֤פֶשׁ הֽ͏ַחַיָּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתְּכֶ֔ם בָּע֧וֹף בַּבְּהֵמָ֛ה וּֽבְכָל־ חַיַּ֥ת הָאָ֖רֶץ אִתְּכֶ֑ם מִכֹּל֙ יֹצְאֵ֣י הַתֵּבָ֔ה לְכֹ֖ל חַיַּ֥ת הָאָֽרֶץ׃
units.en: and with every living creature that is with you—birds, domestic animals, and all the wild animals of the earth with you—from all who went out of the ark to every wild animal of the earth.

units.he: וַהֲקִמֹתִ֤י אֶת־ בְּרִיתִי֙ אִתְּכֶ֔ם וְלֹֽא־ יִכָּרֵ֧ת כָּל־ בָּשָׂ֛ר ע֖וֹד מִמֵּ֣י הַמַּבּ֑וּל וְלֹֽא־ יִהְיֶ֥ה ע֛וֹד מַבּ֖וּל לְשַׁחֵ֥ת הָאָֽרֶץ׃
units.en: I will establish My covenant with you: all flesh will never again be cut off by floodwaters, and there will never again be a flood to destroy the earth.”

units.he: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֗ים זֹ֤את אֽוֹת־ הַבְּרִית֙ אֲשֶׁר־ אֲנִ֣י נֹתֵ֗ן בֵּינִי֙ וּבֵ֣ינֵיכֶ֔ם וּבֵ֛ין כָּל־ נֶ֥פֶשׁ חַיָּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתְּכֶ֑ם לְדֹרֹ֖ת עוֹלָֽם׃
units.en: God said: “This is the sign of the covenant that I am giving between Me and you and every living creature with you, for everlasting generations.

units.he: אֶת־ קַשְׁתִּ֕י נָתַ֖תִּי בֶּֽעָנָ֑ן וְהָֽיְתָה֙ לְא֣וֹת בְּרִ֔ית בֵּינִ֖י וּבֵ֥ין הָאָֽרֶץ׃
units.en: I have set My bow in the cloud, and it will be a sign of the covenant between Me and the earth.

units.he: וְהָיָ֕ה בְּעֽ͏ַנְנִ֥י עָנָ֖ן עַל־ הָאָ֑רֶץ וְנִרְאֲתָ֥ה הַקֶּ֖שֶׁת בֶּעָנָֽן׃
units.en: When I bring clouds over the earth and the bow appears in the cloud,
meaningNotes: The “when” clause is completed by “I will remember” in the following verse.
displayMeaningNotes: The “when” clause is completed by “I will remember” in the following verse.

units.he: וְזָכַרְתִּ֣י אֶת־ בְּרִיתִ֗י אֲשֶׁ֤ר בֵּינִי֙ וּבֵ֣ינֵיכֶ֔ם וּבֵ֛ין כָּל־ נֶ֥פֶשׁ חַיָּ֖ה בְּכָל־ בָּשָׂ֑ר וְלֹֽא־ יִֽהְיֶ֨ה ע֤וֹד הַמַּ֙יִם֙ לְמַבּ֔וּל לְשַׁחֵ֖ת כָּל־ בָּשָֽׂר׃
units.en: I will remember My covenant between Me and you and every living creature of all flesh. The waters will never again become a flood to destroy all flesh.

units.he: וְהָיְתָ֥ה הַקֶּ֖שֶׁת בֶּֽעָנָ֑ן וּרְאִיתִ֗יהָ לִזְכֹּר֙ בְּרִ֣ית עוֹלָ֔ם בֵּ֣ין אֱלֹהִ֔ים וּבֵין֙ כָּל־ נֶ֣פֶשׁ חַיָּ֔ה בְּכָל־ בָּשָׂ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃
units.en: The bow will be in the cloud, and I will see it, to remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh upon the earth.”

units.he: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶל־ נֹ֑חַ זֹ֤את אֽוֹת־ הַבְּרִית֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֲקִמֹ֔תִי בֵּינִ֕י וּבֵ֥ין כָּל־ בָּשָׂ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃
units.en: God said to Noach: “This is the sign of the covenant that I have established between Me and all flesh upon the earth.”

units.he: וַיִּֽהְי֣וּ בְנֵי־ נֹ֗חַ הַיֹּֽצְאִים֙ מִן־ הַתֵּבָ֔ה שֵׁ֖ם וְחָ֣ם וָיָ֑פֶת וְחָ֕ם ה֖וּא אֲבִ֥י כְנָֽעַן׃
units.en: The sons of Noach who went out of the ark were Shem, Cham, and Yefes; Cham was the father of Canaan.

units.he: שְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה אֵ֖לֶּה בְּנֵי־ נֹ֑חַ וּמֵאֵ֖לֶּה נָֽפְצָ֥ה כָל־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃
units.en: These three were the sons of Noach, and from these the population spread over the whole earth.

units.he: וַיָּ֥חֶל נֹ֖חַ אִ֣ישׁ הֽ͏ָאֲדָמָ֑ה וַיִּטַּ֖ע כָּֽרֶם׃
units.en: Noach, a man of the soil, began and planted a vineyard.
meaningNotes: “Began” renders וַיָּחֶל; the verse does not state an additional act after “began” apart from planting.
displayMeaningNotes: “Began” renders וַיָּחֶל; the verse does not state an additional act after “began” apart from planting.

units.he: וַיֵּ֥שְׁתְּ מִן־ הַיַּ֖יִן וַיִּשְׁכָּ֑ר וַיִּתְגַּ֖ל בְּת֥וֹךְ אָהֳלֹֽה׃
units.en: He drank some of the wine, became drunk, and uncovered himself inside his tent.

units.he: וַיַּ֗רְא חָ֚ם אֲבִ֣י כְנַ֔עַן אֵ֖ת עֶרְוַ֣ת אָבִ֑יו וַיַּגֵּ֥ד לִשְׁנֵֽי־ אֶחָ֖יו בַּחֽוּץ׃
units.en: Cham, the father of Canaan, saw his father’s nakedness and told his two brothers outside.

units.he: וַיִּקַּח֩ שֵׁ֨ם וָיֶ֜פֶת אֶת־ הַשִּׂמְלָ֗ה וַיָּשִׂ֙ימוּ֙ עַל־ שְׁכֶ֣ם שְׁנֵיהֶ֔ם וַיֵּֽלְכוּ֙ אֲחֹ֣רַנִּ֔ית וַיְכַסּ֕וּ אֵ֖ת עֶרְוַ֣ת אֲבִיהֶ֑ם וּפְנֵיהֶם֙ אֲחֹ֣רַנִּ֔ית וְעֶרְוַ֥ת אֲבִיהֶ֖ם לֹ֥א רָאֽוּ׃
units.en: Shem and Yefes took the garment, put it over both their shoulders, walked backward, and covered their father’s nakedness. Their faces were turned backward, and they did not see their father’s nakedness.

units.he: וַיִּ֥יקֶץ נֹ֖חַ מִיֵּינ֑וֹ וַיֵּ֕דַע אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־ עָ֥שָׂה־ ל֖וֹ בְּנ֥וֹ הַקָּטָֽן׃
units.en: Noach awoke from his wine and knew what his younger son had done to him.
meaningNotes: “Younger” can also be rendered “youngest”; the verse itself does not spell out the act referred to.
displayMeaningNotes: “Younger” can also be rendered “youngest”; the verse itself does not spell out the act referred to.

units.he: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אָר֣וּר כְּנָ֑עַן עֶ֥בֶד עֲבָדִ֖ים יִֽהְיֶ֥ה לְאֶחָֽיו׃
units.en: He said: “Cursed is Canaan; a slave of slaves shall he be to his brothers.”
meaningNotes: The curse is pronounced on Canaan, the named figure in this account; it is not an authorization of slavery or a racial classification.
displayMeaningNotes: The curse is pronounced on Canaan, the named figure in this account; it is not an authorization of slavery or a racial classification.

units.he: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר בָּר֥וּךְ יְהֹוָ֖ה אֱלֹ֣הֵי שֵׁ֑ם וִיהִ֥י כְנַ֖עַן עֶ֥בֶד לָֽמוֹ׃
units.en: He said: “Blessed is the LORD, the God of Shem; and let Canaan be a slave to them.

units.he: יַ֤פְתְּ אֱלֹהִים֙ לְיֶ֔פֶת וְיִשְׁכֹּ֖ן בְּאָֽהֳלֵי־ שֵׁ֑ם וִיהִ֥י כְנַ֖עַן עֶ֥בֶד לָֽמוֹ׃
units.en: May God enlarge Yefes, and may he dwell in the tents of Shem; and let Canaan be a slave to them.”
meaningNotes: The subject of “dwell” is not explicitly repeated; it can be understood as God or Yefes. The Targum gives its own explicit interpretation separately.
displayMeaningNotes: The subject of “dwell” is not explicitly repeated; it can be understood as God or Yefes. The Targum gives its own explicit interpretation separately.

units.he: וֽ͏ַיְחִי־ נֹ֖חַ אַחַ֣ר הַמַּבּ֑וּל שְׁלֹ֤שׁ מֵאוֹת֙ שָׁנָ֔ה וֽ͏ַחֲמִשִּׁ֖ים שָׁנָֽה׃
units.en: Noach lived after the flood for three hundred and fifty years.

units.he: וַיִּֽהְיוּ֙ כָּל־ יְמֵי־ נֹ֔חַ תְּשַׁ֤ע מֵאוֹת֙ שָׁנָ֔ה וַחֲמִשִּׁ֖ים שָׁנָ֑ה וַיָּמֹֽת׃
units.en: All the days of Noach were nine hundred and fifty years, and he died.

units.he: וְאֵ֙לֶּה֙ תּוֹלְדֹ֣ת בְּנֵי־ נֹ֔חַ שֵׁ֖ם חָ֣ם וָיָ֑פֶת וַיִּוָּלְד֥וּ לָהֶ֛ם בָּנִ֖ים אַחַ֥ר הַמַּבּֽוּל׃
units.en: These are the generations of the sons of Noach: Shem, Cham, and Yefes. Sons were born to them after the flood.

units.he: בְּנֵ֣י יֶ֔פֶת גֹּ֣מֶר וּמָג֔וֹג וּמָדַ֖י וְיָוָ֣ן וְתֻבָ֑ל וּמֶ֖שֶׁךְ וְתִירָֽס׃
units.en: The sons of Yefes were Gomer, Magog, Madai, Yavan, Tuval, Meshech, and Tiras.

units.he: וּבְנֵ֖י גֹּ֑מֶר אַשְׁכֲּנַ֥ז וְרִיפַ֖ת וְתֹגַרְמָֽה׃
units.en: The sons of Gomer were Ashkenaz, Rifas, and Togarmuh.

units.he: וּבְנֵ֥י יָוָ֖ן אֱלִישָׁ֣ה וְתַרְשִׁ֑ישׁ כִּתִּ֖ים וְדֹדָנִֽים׃
units.en: The sons of Yavan were Elishuh, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.

units.he: מֵ֠אֵלֶּה נִפְרְד֞וּ אִיֵּ֤י הַגּוֹיִם֙ בְּאַרְצֹתָ֔ם אִ֖ישׁ לִלְשֹׁנ֑וֹ לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֖ם בְּגוֹיֵהֶֽם׃
units.en: From these the coastland nations separated in their lands, each according to its language, according to their families, within their nations.

units.he: וּבְנֵ֖י חָ֑ם כּ֥וּשׁ וּמִצְרַ֖יִם וּפ֥וּט וּכְנָֽעַן׃
units.en: The sons of Cham were Cush, Mitzrayim, Put, and Canaan.

units.he: וּבְנֵ֣י כ֔וּשׁ סְבָא֙ וֽ͏ַחֲוִילָ֔ה וְסַבְתָּ֥ה וְרַעְמָ֖ה וְסַבְתְּכָ֑א וּבְנֵ֥י רַעְמָ֖ה שְׁבָ֥א וּדְדָֽן׃
units.en: The sons of Cush were Seva, Chaviluh, Savtuh, Raamuh, and Savtecha; the sons of Raamuh were Sheva and Dedan.

units.he: וְכ֖וּשׁ יָלַ֣ד אֶת־ נִמְרֹ֑ד ה֣וּא הֵחֵ֔ל לֽ͏ִהְי֥וֹת גִּבֹּ֖ר בָּאָֽרֶץ׃
units.en: Cush fathered Nimrod; he began to be a mighty man upon the earth.

units.he: הֽוּא־ הָיָ֥ה גִבֹּֽר־ צַ֖יִד לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה עַל־ כֵּן֙ יֵֽאָמַ֔ר כְּנִמְרֹ֛ד גִּבּ֥וֹר צַ֖יִד לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
units.en: He was a mighty hunter before the LORD; therefore it is said, “Like Nimrod, a mighty hunter before the LORD.”

units.he: וַתְּהִ֨י רֵאשִׁ֤ית מַמְלַכְתּוֹ֙ בָּבֶ֔ל וְאֶ֖רֶךְ וְאַכַּ֣ד וְכַלְנֵ֑ה בְּאֶ֖רֶץ שִׁנְעָֽר׃
units.en: The beginning of his kingdom was Babel, Erech, Akkad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.

units.he: מִן־ הָאָ֥רֶץ הַהִ֖וא יָצָ֣א אַשּׁ֑וּר וַיִּ֙בֶן֙ אֶת־ נִ֣ינְוֵ֔ה וְאֶת־ רְחֹבֹ֥ת עִ֖יר וְאֶת־ כָּֽלַח׃
units.en: From that land Ashur went out and built Nineveh, Rechovos Ir, and Calach,
meaningNotes: Alternatively, Ashur can be read as the destination, “he went out to Assyria”; the source leaves the grammatical interpretation open.
displayMeaningNotes: Alternatively, Ashur can be read as the destination, “he went out to Assyria”; the source leaves the grammatical interpretation open.

units.he: וְֽאֶת־ רֶ֔סֶן בֵּ֥ין נִֽינְוֵ֖ה וּבֵ֣ין כָּ֑לַח הִ֖וא הָעִ֥יר הַגְּדֹלָֽה׃
units.en: and Resen between Nineveh and Calach; it is the great city.
meaningNotes: The antecedent of “it is the great city” is not expressly named.
displayMeaningNotes: The antecedent of “it is the great city” is not expressly named.

units.he: וּמִצְרַ֡יִם יָלַ֞ד אֶת־ לוּדִ֧ים וְאֶת־ עֲנָמִ֛ים וְאֶת־ לְהָבִ֖ים וְאֶת־ נַפְתֻּחִֽים׃
units.en: Mitzrayim fathered the Ludim, Anamim, Lehavim, and Naftuchim,

units.he: וְֽאֶת־ פַּתְרֻסִ֞ים וְאֶת־ כַּסְלֻחִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָצְא֥וּ מִשָּׁ֛ם פְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים וְאֶת־ כַּפְתֹּרִֽים׃
units.en: and the Patrusim, the Casluchim—from whom the Philistines came forth—and the Caftorim.

units.he: וּכְנַ֗עַן יָלַ֛ד אֶת־ צִידֹ֥ן בְּכֹר֖וֹ וְאֶת־ חֵֽת׃
units.en: Canaan fathered Tzidon his firstborn, and Ches,

units.he: וְאֶת־ הַיְבוּסִי֙ וְאֶת־ הָ֣אֱמֹרִ֔י וְאֵ֖ת הַגִּרְגָּשִֽׁי׃
units.en: and the Jebusites, Amorites, and Girgashites,

units.he: וְאֶת־ הֽ͏ַחִוִּ֥י וְאֶת־ הֽ͏ַעַרְקִ֖י וְאֶת־ הַסִּינִֽי׃
units.en: and the Hivites, Arkites, and Sinites,

units.he: וְאֶת־ הֽ͏ָאַרְוָדִ֥י וְאֶת־ הַצְּמָרִ֖י וְאֶת־ הֽ͏ַחֲמָתִ֑י וְאַחַ֣ר נָפֹ֔צוּ מִשְׁפְּח֖וֹת הֽ͏ַכְּנַעֲנִֽי׃
units.en: and the Arvadites, Tzemarites, and Chamasites. Afterward the families of the Canaanites dispersed.

units.he: וֽ͏ַיְהִ֞י גְּב֤וּל הֽ͏ַכְּנַעֲנִי֙ מִצִּידֹ֔ן בֹּאֲכָ֥ה גְרָ֖רָה עַד־ עַזָּ֑ה בֹּאֲכָ֞ה סְדֹ֧מָה וַעֲמֹרָ֛ה וְאַדְמָ֥ה וּצְבֹיִ֖ם עַד־ לָֽשַׁע׃
units.en: The boundary of the Canaanites extended from Tzidon toward Gerar as far as Azzuh, and toward Sedom, Amoruh, Admuh, and Tzevoyim as far as Lashuh.

units.he: אֵ֣לֶּה בְנֵי־ חָ֔ם לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֖ם לִלְשֹֽׁנֹתָ֑ם בְּאַרְצֹתָ֖ם בְּגוֹיֵהֶֽם׃
units.en: These are the sons of Cham, according to their families and languages, in their lands and nations.

units.he: וּלְשֵׁ֥ם יֻלַּ֖ד גַּם־ ה֑וּא אֲבִי֙ כָּל־ בְּנֵי־ עֵ֔בֶר אֲחִ֖י יֶ֥פֶת הַגָּדֽוֹל׃
units.en: Children were also born to Shem, the ancestor of all the children of Ever, the brother of Yefes the elder.
meaningNotes: The Hebrew can also be understood as “the elder brother of Yefes”; the placement of “elder” is interpretively ambiguous.
displayMeaningNotes: The Hebrew can also be understood as “the elder brother of Yefes”; the placement of “elder” is interpretively ambiguous.

units.he: בְּנֵ֥י שֵׁ֖ם עֵילָ֣ם וְאַשּׁ֑וּר וְאַרְפַּכְשַׁ֖ד וְל֥וּד וֽ͏ַאֲרָֽם׃
units.en: The sons of Shem were Elam, Ashur, Arpachshad, Lud, and Aram.

units.he: וּבְנֵ֖י אֲרָ֑ם ע֥וּץ וְח֖וּל וְגֶ֥תֶר וָמַֽשׁ׃
units.en: The sons of Aram were Utz, Chul, Geser, and Mash.

units.he: וְאַרְפַּכְשַׁ֖ד יָלַ֣ד אֶת־ שָׁ֑לַח וְשֶׁ֖לַח יָלַ֥ד אֶת־ עֵֽבֶר׃
units.en: Arpachshad fathered Shelach, and Shelach fathered Ever.

units.he: וּלְעֵ֥בֶר יֻלַּ֖ד שְׁנֵ֣י בָנִ֑ים שֵׁ֣ם הֽ͏ָאֶחָ֞ד פֶּ֗לֶג כִּ֤י בְיָמָיו֙ נִפְלְגָ֣ה הָאָ֔רֶץ וְשֵׁ֥ם אָחִ֖יו יָקְטָֽן׃
units.en: Two sons were born to Ever: the name of one was Peleg, because in his days the earth was divided; his brother’s name was Yoktan.
meaningNotes: Peleg’s name echoes the verb “was divided”; the verse does not specify the division’s mechanism.
displayMeaningNotes: Peleg’s name echoes the verb “was divided”; the verse does not specify the division’s mechanism.

units.he: וְיָקְטָ֣ן יָלַ֔ד אֶת־ אַלְמוֹדָ֖ד וְאֶת־ שָׁ֑לֶף וְאֶת־ חֲצַרְמָ֖וֶת וְאֶת־ יָֽרַח׃
units.en: Yoktan fathered Almodad, Shalef, Chatzarmaves, and Yerach,

units.he: וְאֶת־ הֲדוֹרָ֥ם וְאֶת־ אוּזָ֖ל וְאֶת־ דִּקְלָֽה׃
units.en: and Hadoram, Uzal, and Diklah,

units.he: וְאֶת־ עוֹבָ֥ל וְאֶת־ אֲבִֽימָאֵ֖ל וְאֶת־ שְׁבָֽא׃
units.en: and Oval, Avimael, and Sheva,

units.he: וְאֶת־ אוֹפִ֥ר וְאֶת־ חֲוִילָ֖ה וְאֶת־ יוֹבָ֑ב כָּל־ אֵ֖לֶּה בְּנֵ֥י יָקְטָֽן׃
units.en: and Ofir, Chaviluh, and Yovav. All these were the sons of Yoktan.

units.he: וֽ͏ַיְהִ֥י מוֹשָׁבָ֖ם מִמֵּשָׁ֑א בֹּאֲכָ֥ה סְפָ֖רָה הַ֥ר הַקֶּֽדֶם׃
units.en: Their dwelling extended from Maishuh toward Sefar, the mountain of the east.

units.he: אֵ֣לֶּה בְנֵי־ שֵׁ֔ם לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֖ם לִלְשֹׁנֹתָ֑ם בְּאַרְצֹתָ֖ם לְגוֹיֵהֶֽם׃
units.en: These are the sons of Shem, according to their families and languages, in their lands, according to their nations.

units.he: אֵ֣לֶּה מִשְׁפְּחֹ֧ת בְּנֵי־ נֹ֛חַ לְתוֹלְדֹתָ֖ם בְּגוֹיֵהֶ֑ם וּמֵאֵ֜לֶּה נִפְרְד֧וּ הַגּוֹיִ֛ם בָּאָ֖רֶץ אַחַ֥ר הַמַּבּֽוּל׃
units.en: These are the families of the sons of Noach, according to their generations, in their nations. From these the nations separated upon the earth after the flood.

units.he: וֽ͏ַיְהִ֥י כָל־ הָאָ֖רֶץ שָׂפָ֣ה אֶחָ֑ת וּדְבָרִ֖ים אֲחָדִֽים׃
units.en: The whole earth had one language and common words.
meaningNotes: “Common words” renders “words that were one”; no particular ancient language is named.
displayMeaningNotes: “Common words” renders “words that were one”; no particular ancient language is named.

units.he: וֽ͏ַיְהִ֖י בְּנָסְעָ֣ם מִקֶּ֑דֶם וֽ͏ַיִּמְצְא֥וּ בִקְעָ֛ה בְּאֶ֥רֶץ שִׁנְעָ֖ר וַיֵּ֥שְׁבוּ שָֽׁם׃
units.en: As they traveled from the east, they found a plain in the land of Shinar and settled there.
meaningNotes: “From the east” is the direct directional rendering; “eastward” is another interpretation of מִקֶּדֶם.
displayMeaningNotes: “From the east” is the direct directional rendering; “eastward” is another interpretation of מִקֶּדֶם.

units.he: וַיֹּאמְר֞וּ אִ֣ישׁ אֶל־ רֵעֵ֗הוּ הָ֚בָה נִלְבְּנָ֣ה לְבֵנִ֔ים וְנִשְׂרְפָ֖ה לִשְׂרֵפָ֑ה וַתְּהִ֨י לָהֶ֤ם הַלְּבֵנָה֙ לְאָ֔בֶן וְהַ֣חֵמָ֔ר הָיָ֥ה לָהֶ֖ם לַחֹֽמֶר׃
units.en: They said to one another: “Come, let us make bricks and burn them thoroughly.” Brick served them as stone, and bitumen served them as mortar.
