units.he: וַיֹּאמְר֞וּ הָ֣בָה ׀ נִבְנֶה־ לָּ֣נוּ עִ֗יר וּמִגְדָּל֙ וְרֹאשׁ֣וֹ בַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְנַֽעֲשֶׂה־ לָּ֖נוּ שֵׁ֑ם פֶּן־ נָפ֖וּץ עַל־ פְּנֵ֥י כָל־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃
units.en: They said: “Come, let us build ourselves a city and a tower with its top in the heavens, and make ourselves a name, lest we be scattered over the face of the whole earth.”

units.he: וַיֵּ֣רֶד יְהוָ֔ה לִרְאֹ֥ת אֶת־ הָעִ֖יר וְאֶת־ הַמִּגְדָּ֑ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּנ֖וּ בְּנֵ֥י הָאָדָֽם׃
units.en: The LORD came down to see the city and the tower that human beings had built.

units.he: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֗ה הֵ֣ן עַ֤ם אֶחָד֙ וְשָׂפָ֤ה אַחַת֙ לְכֻלָּ֔ם וְזֶ֖ה הַחִלָּ֣ם לַעֲשׂ֑וֹת וְעַתָּה֙ לֹֽא־ יִבָּצֵ֣ר מֵהֶ֔ם כֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָזְמ֖וּ לֽ͏ַעֲשֽׂוֹת׃
units.en: The LORD said: “They are one people, and all have one language, and this is what they have begun to do. Now nothing that they plan to do will be withheld from them.

units.he: הָ֚בָה נֽ͏ֵרְדָ֔ה וְנָבְלָ֥ה שָׁ֖ם שְׂפָתָ֑ם אֲשֶׁר֙ לֹ֣א יִשְׁמְע֔וּ אִ֖ישׁ שְׂפַ֥ת רֵעֵֽהוּ׃
units.en: Come, let us go down and confuse their language there, so that one will not understand the language of another.”

units.he: וַיָּ֨פֶץ יְהוָ֥ה אֹתָ֛ם מִשָּׁ֖ם עַל־ פְּנֵ֣י כָל־ הָאָ֑רֶץ וֽ͏ַיַּחְדְּל֖וּ לִבְנֹ֥ת הָעִֽיר׃
units.en: The LORD scattered them from there over the face of the whole earth, and they stopped building the city.

units.he: עַל־ כֵּ֞ן קָרָ֤א שְׁמָהּ֙ בָּבֶ֔ל כִּי־ שָׁ֛ם בָּלַ֥ל יְהוָ֖ה שְׂפַ֣ת כָּל־ הָאָ֑רֶץ וּמִשָּׁם֙ הֱפִיצָ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה עַל־ פְּנֵ֖י כָּל־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃
units.en: Therefore its name was called Babel, because there the LORD confused the language of the whole earth; and from there the LORD scattered them over the face of the whole earth.
meaningNotes: Babel is linked in the verse to the Hebrew verb for confusing, בָּלַל.
displayMeaningNotes: Babel is linked in the verse to the Hebrew verb for confusing, בָּלַל.

units.he: אֵ֚לֶּה תּוֹלְדֹ֣ת שֵׁ֔ם שֵׁ֚ם בֶּן־ מְאַ֣ת שָׁנָ֔ה וַיּ֖וֹלֶד אֶת־ אַרְפַּכְשָׁ֑ד שְׁנָתַ֖יִם אַחַ֥ר הַמַּבּֽוּל׃
units.en: These are the generations of Shem. Shem was one hundred years old when he fathered Arpachshad, two years after the flood.

units.he: וֽ͏ַיְחִי־ שֵׁ֗ם אֽ͏ַחֲרֵי֙ הוֹלִיד֣וֹ אֶת־ אַרְפַּכְשָׁ֔ד חֲמֵ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָ֑ה וַיּ֥וֹלֶד בָּנִ֖ים וּבָנֽוֹת׃
units.en: Shem lived five hundred years after fathering Arpachshad, and fathered sons and daughters.

units.he: וְאַרְפַּכְשַׁ֣ד חַ֔י חָמֵ֥שׁ וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֖ים שָׁנָ֑ה וַיּ֖וֹלֶד אֶת־ שָֽׁלַח׃
units.en: Arpachshad lived thirty-five years and fathered Shelach.

units.he: וֽ͏ַיְחִ֣י אַרְפַּכְשַׁ֗ד אֽ͏ַחֲרֵי֙ הוֹלִיד֣וֹ אֶת־ שֶׁ֔לַח שָׁלֹ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֔ים וְאַרְבַּ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָ֑ה וַיּ֥וֹלֶד בָּנִ֖ים וּבָנֽוֹת׃
units.en: Arpachshad lived four hundred and three years after fathering Shelach, and fathered sons and daughters.

units.he: וְשֶׁ֥לַח חַ֖י שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֑ה וַיּ֖וֹלֶד אֶת־ עֵֽבֶר׃
units.en: Shelach lived thirty years and fathered Ever.

units.he: וֽ͏ַיְחִי־ שֶׁ֗לַח אַחֲרֵי֙ הוֹלִיד֣וֹ אֶת־ עֵ֔בֶר שָׁלֹ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֔ים וְאַרְבַּ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָ֑ה וַיּ֥וֹלֶד בָּנִ֖ים וּבָנֽוֹת׃
units.en: Shelach lived four hundred and three years after fathering Ever, and fathered sons and daughters.

units.he: וַֽיְחִי־ עֵ֕בֶר אַרְבַּ֥ע וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֖ים שָׁנָ֑ה וַיּ֖וֹלֶד אֶת־ פָּֽלֶג׃
units.en: Ever lived thirty-four years and fathered Peleg.

units.he: וַֽיְחִי־ עֵ֗בֶר אַחֲרֵי֙ הוֹלִיד֣וֹ אֶת־ פֶּ֔לֶג שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה וְאַרְבַּ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת שָׁנָ֑ה וַיּ֥וֹלֶד בָּנִ֖ים וּבָנֽוֹת׃
units.en: Ever lived four hundred and thirty years after fathering Peleg, and fathered sons and daughters.

units.he: וֽ͏ַיְחִי־ פֶ֖לֶג שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֑ה וַיּ֖וֹלֶד אֶת־ רְעֽוּ׃
units.en: Peleg lived thirty years and fathered Reu.

units.he: וֽ͏ַיְחִי־ פֶ֗לֶג אַחֲרֵי֙ הוֹלִיד֣וֹ אֶת־ רְע֔וּ תֵּ֥שַׁע שָׁנִ֖ים וּמָאתַ֣יִם שָׁנָ֑ה וַיּ֥וֹלֶד בָּנִ֖ים וּבָנֽוֹת׃
units.en: Peleg lived two hundred and nine years after fathering Reu, and fathered sons and daughters.

units.he: וַיְחִ֣י רְע֔וּ שְׁתַּ֥יִם וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֖ים שָׁנָ֑ה וַיּ֖וֹלֶד אֶת־ שְׂרֽוּג׃
units.en: Reu lived thirty-two years and fathered Serug.

units.he: וַיְחִ֣י רְע֗וּ אַחֲרֵי֙ הוֹלִיד֣וֹ אֶת־ שְׂר֔וּג שֶׁ֥בַע שָׁנִ֖ים וּמָאתַ֣יִם שָׁנָ֑ה וַיּ֥וֹלֶד בָּנִ֖ים וּבָנֽוֹת׃
units.en: Reu lived two hundred and seven years after fathering Serug, and fathered sons and daughters.

units.he: וַיְחִ֥י שְׂר֖וּג שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֑ה וַיּ֖וֹלֶד אֶת־ נָחֽוֹר׃
units.en: Serug lived thirty years and fathered Nachor.

units.he: וַיְחִ֣י שְׂר֗וּג אַחֲרֵ֛י הוֹלִיד֥וֹ אֶת־ נָח֖וֹר מָאתַ֣יִם שָׁנָ֑ה וַיּ֥וֹלֶד בָּנִ֖ים וּבָנֽוֹת׃
units.en: Serug lived two hundred years after fathering Nachor, and fathered sons and daughters.

units.he: וַיְחִ֣י נָח֔וֹר תֵּ֥שַׁע וְעֶשְׂרִ֖ים שָׁנָ֑ה וַיּ֖וֹלֶד אֶת־ תָּֽרַח׃
units.en: Nachor lived twenty-nine years and fathered Terach.

units.he: וַיְחִ֣י נָח֗וֹר אַחֲרֵי֙ הוֹלִיד֣וֹ אֶת־ תֶּ֔רַח תְּשַֽׁע־ עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה שָׁנָ֖ה וּמְאַ֣ת שָׁנָ֑ה וַיּ֥וֹלֶד בָּנִ֖ים וּבָנֽוֹת׃
units.en: Nachor lived one hundred and nineteen years after fathering Terach, and fathered sons and daughters.

units.he: וֽ͏ַיְחִי־ תֶ֖רַח שִׁבְעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֑ה וַיּ֙וֹלֶד֙ אֶת־ אַבְרָ֔ם אֶת־ נָח֖וֹר וְאֶת־ הָרָֽן׃
units.en: Terach lived seventy years and fathered Avram, Nachor, and Haran.

units.he: וְאֵ֙לֶּה֙ תּוֹלְדֹ֣ת תֶּ֔רַח תֶּ֚רַח הוֹלִ֣יד אֶת־ אַבְרָ֔ם אֶת־ נָח֖וֹר וְאֶת־ הָרָ֑ן וְהָרָ֖ן הוֹלִ֥יד אֶת־ לֽוֹט׃
units.en: These are the generations of Terach: Terach fathered Avram, Nachor, and Haran; Haran fathered Lot.

units.he: וַיָּ֣מָת הָרָ֔ן עַל־ פְּנֵ֖י תֶּ֣רַח אָבִ֑יו בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מוֹלַדְתּ֖וֹ בְּא֥וּר כַּשְׂדִּֽים׃
units.en: Haran died in the presence of Terach his father, in the land of his birth, in Ur of the Chaldeans.
meaningNotes: “In the presence of” also conveys dying during his father’s lifetime; the verse does not specify the cause of death.
displayMeaningNotes: “In the presence of” also conveys dying during his father’s lifetime; the verse does not specify the cause of death.

units.he: וַיִּקַּ֨ח אַבְרָ֧ם וְנָח֛וֹר לָהֶ֖ם נָשִׁ֑ים שֵׁ֤ם אֵֽשֶׁת־ אַבְרָם֙ שָׂרָ֔י וְשֵׁ֤ם אֵֽשֶׁת־ נָחוֹר֙ מִלְכָּ֔ה בַּת־ הָרָ֥ן אֲבִֽי־ מִלְכָּ֖ה וֽ͏ַאֲבִ֥י יִסְכָּֽה׃
units.en: Avram and Nachor took wives for themselves. The name of Avram’s wife was Sarai, and the name of Nachor’s wife was Milkah, the daughter of Haran, the father of Milkah and the father of Yiskuh.

units.he: וַתְּהִ֥י שָׂרַ֖י עֲקָרָ֑ה אֵ֥ין לָ֖הּ וָלָֽד׃
units.en: Sarai was barren; she had no child.

units.he: וַיִּקַּ֨ח תֶּ֜רַח אֶת־ אַבְרָ֣ם בְּנ֗וֹ וְאֶת־ ל֤וֹט בֶּן־ הָרָן֙ בֶּן־ בְּנ֔וֹ וְאֵת֙ שָׂרַ֣י כַּלָּת֔וֹ אֵ֖שֶׁת אַבְרָ֣ם בְּנ֑וֹ וַיֵּצְא֨וּ אִתָּ֜ם מֵא֣וּר כַּשְׂדִּ֗ים לָלֶ֙כֶת֙ אַ֣רְצָה כְּנַ֔עַן וַיָּבֹ֥אוּ עַד־ חָרָ֖ן וַיֵּ֥שְׁבוּ שָֽׁם׃
units.en: Terach took Avram his son, Lot the son of Haran, his grandson, and Sarai his daughter-in-law, the wife of Avram his son. They went out with them from Ur of the Chaldeans to go to the land of Canaan. They came as far as Charan and settled there.

units.he: וַיִּהְי֣וּ יְמֵי־ תֶ֔רַח חָמֵ֥שׁ שָׁנִ֖ים וּמָאתַ֣יִם שָׁנָ֑ה וַיָּ֥מָת תֶּ֖רַח בְּחָרָֽן׃
units.en: The days of Terach were two hundred and five years, and Terach died in Charan.

units.he: וּמַלֵּיל יְיָ עִם נֹחַ לְמֵימָר:
units.en: The LORD spoke with Noach, saying:

units.he: פּוּק מִן תֵּבוֹתָא אַתְּ וְאִתְּתָךְ וּבְנָךְ וּנְשֵׁי בְנָךְ עִמָּךְ:
units.en: “Go out of the ark, you and your wife, your sons and your sons’ wives with you.

units.he: כָּל חַיְתָא דִּעִמָּךְ מִכָּל בִּשְׂרָא בְּעוֹפָא וּבִבְעִירָא וּבְכָל רִחֲשָׁא דְּרָחֵשׁ עַל אַרְעָא אַפֵּיק עִמָּךְ וְיִתְיַלְּדוּן בְּאַרְעָא וְיִפְּשׁוּן וְיִסְגּוּן עַל אַרְעָא:
units.en: Take out with you all the living creatures that are with you, of all flesh: the birds, the domestic animals, and all the moving creatures that move upon the earth. Let them breed upon the earth, increase, and multiply upon the earth.”

units.he: וּנְפַק נֹחַ וּבְנוֹהִי וְאִתְּתֵיהּ וּנְשֵׁי בְנוֹהִי עִמֵּיהּ:
units.en: Noach came out, and his sons, his wife, and his sons’ wives accompanied him.

units.he: כָּל חַיְתָא כָּל רִחֲשָׁא וְכָל עוֹפָא כֹּל דְּרָחֵשׁ עַל אַרְעָא לְזַרְעֲיָתְהוֹן נְפָקוּ מִן תֵּבוֹתָא:
units.en: All the wild animals, all the moving creatures, and all the birds—everything that moves upon the earth—came out of the ark according to their breeds.

units.he: וּבְנָא נֹחַ מַדְבְּחָא קֳדָם יְיָ וּנְסִיב מִכֹּל בְּעִירָא דַכְיָא וּמִכֹּל עוֹפָא דְכֵי וְאַסֵּיק עֲלָוָן בְּמִדְבְּחָא:
units.en: Noach built an altar before the LORD. He took of every clean animal and every clean bird, and brought up burnt offerings upon the altar.

units.he: וְקַבִּיל יְיָ בְּרַעֲוָא יָת קוּרְבָּנֵיהּ וַאֲמַר יְיָ בְּמֵימְרֵיהּ לָא אוֹסֵף לְמֵילַט עוֹד יָת אַרְעָא בְּדִיל חוֹבֵי אֱנָשָׁא אֲרֵי יִצְרָא לִבָּא דֶאֱנָשָׁא בִּישׁ מִזְּעִירֵיהּ וְלָא אוֹסֵף עוֹד לְמִמְחֵי יָת כָּל דְּחַי כְּמָא דְעָבְדִית:
units.en: The LORD accepted his offering with favor, and the LORD said by His word: “I will not again curse the earth because of the sins of humankind, for the inclination of the human heart is evil from its youth. I will not again strike down everything that lives as I have done.
meaningNotes: The Targum speaks of accepting an offering with favor and of a declaration by His word, rather than repeating the Bible’s smell and heart imagery.
displayMeaningNotes: The Targum speaks of accepting an offering with favor and of a declaration by His word, rather than repeating the Bible’s smell and heart imagery.

units.he: עוֹד כָּל יוֹמֵי אַרְעָא זְרוֹעָא וַחֲצָדָא וְקוֹרָא וְחוֹמָא וְקַיְטָא וְסִתְוָא וִימָם וְלֵילְיָא לָא יִבְטְלוּן:
units.en: For all the remaining days of the earth, sowing and reaping, cold and heat, summer and winter, daytime and nighttime, will not come to an end.”

units.he: וּבָרִיךְ יְיָ יָת נֹח וְיָת בְּנוֹהִי וַאֲמַר לְהוֹן פּוּשׁוּ וּסְגוּ וּמְלוּ יָת אַרְעָא:
units.en: The LORD blessed Noach and his sons, and said to them: “Increase and multiply, and fill the earth.

units.he: וְדַחֲלַתְכוֹן וְאֵימַתְכוֹן תְּהֵי עַל כָּל חֵוַת אַרְעָא וְעַל כָּל עוֹפָא דִשְׁמַיָּא בְּכֹל דִּי תַרְחֵישׁ אַרְעָא וּבְכָל נוּנֵי יַמָּא בְּיֶדְכוֹן יְהוֹן מְסִירִין:
units.en: The fear and awe of you will be upon all the wild animals of the earth and all the birds of the heavens, upon everything with which the earth teems and all the fish of the sea; they will be delivered into your hands.

units.he: כָּל רִחֲשָׁא דְּהוּא חַי לְכוֹן יְהֵי לְמֵיכָל כִּירוֹק עִשְׂבָּא יְהָבִית לְכוֹן יָת כֹּלָּא:
units.en: Every moving creature that lives shall be yours to eat; like the green plants, I have given you everything.

units.he: בְּרַם בִּשְׂרָא בְּנַפְשֵׁיהּ דְּמֵיהּ לָא תֵכְלוּן:
units.en: However, flesh with its life—its blood—you shall not eat.

units.he: וּבְרַם יָת דִּמְכוֹן לְנַפְשָׁתֵיכוֹן אֶתְבַּע מִיַּד כָּל חַיְתָא אֶתְבְּעִנֵּיהּ וּמִיַּד אֱנָשָׁא מִיַּד גְּבַר דְּיֵשׁוֹד יָת דְּמָא דַאֲחוֹהִי אֶתְבַּע יָת נַפְשָׁא דֶאֱנָשָׁא:
units.en: However, I will demand an accounting for your blood, for your lives. From every animal I will demand it, and from humankind—from the man who sheds his brother’s blood—I will demand an accounting for human life.

units.he: דְּיֵשׁוֹד דְּמָא דֶאֱנָשָׁא בְּסַהֲדִין עַל מֵימַר דַּיָּנַיָּא דְּמֵיהּ יִתְּשָׁד אֲרֵי בְּצַלְמָא דַיְיָ עֲבַד יָת אֱנָשָׁא:
units.en: Whoever sheds human blood, with witnesses, by the pronouncement of the judges his blood shall be shed, for in the image of the LORD He made humankind.
meaningNotes: The Targum expressly requires witnesses and a judicial pronouncement; it does not authorize private retaliation.
displayMeaningNotes: The Targum expressly requires witnesses and a judicial pronouncement; it does not authorize private retaliation.

units.he: וְאַתּוּן פּוּשׁוּ וּסְגוּ אִתְיְלִידוּ בְאַרְעָא וּסְגוּ בַהּ:
units.en: As for you, increase and multiply; reproduce upon the earth, and multiply in it.”

units.he: וַאֲמַר יְיָ לְנֹחַ וְלִבְנוֹהִי עִמֵּיהּ לְמֵימָר:
units.en: The LORD said to Noach and to his sons with him:

units.he: וַאֲנָא הָא אֲנָא מֵקִים יָת קְיָמִי עִמְּכוֹן וְעִם בְּנֵיכוֹן בַּתְרֵיכוֹן:
units.en: “As for Me, I am establishing My covenant with you and with your children after you,

units.he: וְעִם כָּל נַפְשָׁא חַיְתָא דְּעִמְּכוֹן בְּעוֹפָא בִבְעִירָא וּבְכָל חֵיוַת אַרְעָא דְּעִמְּכוֹן מִכֹּל נַפְקֵי תֵבוֹתָא לְכֹל חַיַּת אַרְעָא:
units.en: and with every living creature with you: birds, domestic animals, and all the wild animals of the earth with you, from all that came out of the ark to every wild animal of the earth.

units.he: וְאָקֵם יָת קְיָמִי עִמְּכוֹן וְלָא יִשְׁתֵּיצֵי כָל בִּשְׂרָא עוֹד מִמֵּי טוֹפָנָא וְלָא יְהֵי עוֹד טוֹפָנָא לְחַבָּלָא אַרְעָא:
units.en: I will establish My covenant with you, and all flesh will no longer be destroyed by floodwaters; there will no longer be a flood to destroy the earth.”

units.he: וַאֲמַר יְיָ דָּא אָת קְיָם דִּי אֲנָא יָהֵב בֵּין מֵימְרִי וּבֵינֵיכוֹן וּבֵין כָּל נַפְשָׁא חַיְתָא דִּי עִמְּכוֹן לְדָרֵי עַלְמָא:
units.en: The LORD said: “This is the covenant-sign that I give between My word and you and every living creature with you, for everlasting generations.
meaningNotes: The Targum’s “My word” is retained here and in the following covenant clauses.
displayMeaningNotes: The Targum uses “My word” here and in the following covenant clauses.

units.he: יָת קַשְׁתִּי יְהָבִית בַּעֲנָנָא וּתְהִי לְאָת קְיָם בֵּין מֵימְרִי וּבֵין אַרְעָא:
units.en: I have placed My bow in the cloud, and it shall be a covenant-sign between My word and the earth.

units.he: וִיהִי בַּעֲנָנוּתִי עֲנָנָא עַל אַרְעָא וְתִתְחֲזֵי קַשְׁתָּא בַּעֲנָנָא:
units.en: When I cover the earth with cloud, and the bow is seen in the cloud,

units.he: וּדְכִירְנָא יָת קְיָמִי דִּי בֵין מֵימְרִי וּבֵינֵיכוֹן וּבֵין כָּל נַפְשָׁא חַיְתָא בְּכָל בִּשְׂרָא וְלָא יְהֵא עוֹד מַיָּא לְטוֹפָנָא לְחַבָּלָא כָל בִּשְׂרָא:
units.en: I will remember My covenant that is between My word and you and every living creature of all flesh. Water shall no longer become a flood to destroy all flesh.

units.he: וּתְהֵי קַשְׁתָּא בַּעֲנָנָא וְאֵחֲזִנַּהּ לְמִדְכַּר קְיַם עָלָם בֵּין מֵימְרָא דַיְיָ וּבֵין כָּל נַפְשָׁא חַיְתָא בְּכָל בִּשְׂרָא דִּי עַל אַרְעָא:
units.en: The bow shall be in the cloud, and I will see it, to remember the everlasting covenant between the word of the LORD and every living creature of all flesh upon the earth.”

units.he: וַאֲמַר יְיָ לְנֹחַ דָּא אָת קְיָם דִּי אֲקֵמִית בֵּין מֵימְרִי וּבֵין כָּל בִּשְׂרָא דִּי עַל אַרְעָא:
units.en: The LORD said to Noach: “This is the covenant-sign that I have established between My word and all flesh upon the earth.”

units.he: וַהֲווֹ בְנֵי נֹחַ דִּי נְפָקוּ מִן תֵּבוֹתָא שֵׁם וְחָם וָיָפֶת וְחָם הוּא אֲבוּהִי דִכְנָעַן:
units.en: The sons of Noach who came out of the ark were Shem, Cham, and Yefes; Cham was Canaan’s father.

units.he: תְּלָתָא אִלֵּין בְּנֵי נֹחַ וּמֵאִלֵּין אִתְבַּדָּרוּ כָּל אַרְעָא:
units.en: These three were Noach’s sons, and from them [the inhabitants of] the whole earth dispersed.
meaningNotes: The bracket supplies the inhabitants intended by “the whole earth,” not a new source noun.
displayMeaningNotes: The bracket supplies the inhabitants intended by “the whole earth,” not a new source noun.

units.he: וְשָׁרֵי נֹחַ גְּבַר פָּלַח בְּאַרְעָא וּנְצִיב כַּרְמָא:
units.en: Noach, a man who worked the earth, began and planted a vineyard.

units.he: וּשְׁתִי מִן חַמְרָא וּרְוִי וְאִתְגְּלִי בְּגוֹ מַשְׁכְּנֵיהּ:
units.en: He drank from the wine and became intoxicated, and was uncovered within his dwelling.

units.he: וַחֲזָא חָם אֲבוּהִי דִכְנַעַן יָת עֶרְיְתָא דַאֲבוּהִי וְחַוִּי לִתְרֵין אֲחוֹהִי בְּשׁוּקָא:
units.en: Cham, Canaan’s father, saw his father’s nakedness and told his two brothers in the open place outside.

units.he: וּנְסֵיב שֵׁם וָיֶפֶת יָת כְּסוּתָא וְשַׁוִּיוּ עַל כְּתַף תַּרְוֵיהוֹן וַאֲזָלוּ מְחַזְּרִין וַחֲפִיאוּ יָת עֶרְיְתָא דַאֲבוּהוֹן וְאַפֵּיהוֹן מְחַזְּרִין וְעֶרְיְתָא דַאֲבוּהוֹן לָא חֲזוֹ:
units.en: Shem and Yefes took a covering and placed it on both their shoulders. They walked backward and covered their father’s nakedness; their faces were turned backward, and they did not see their father’s nakedness.

units.he: וְאִתְּעַר נֹחַ מֵחַמְרֵיהּ וִידַע יָת דִּי עֲבַד לֵיהּ בְּרֵיהּ זְעֵירָא:
units.en: Noach awoke from his wine and learned what his younger son had done to him.

units.he: וַאֲמַר לִיט כְּנָעַן עֶבֶד פָּלַח עַבְדִין יְהֵי לַאֲחוֹהִי:
units.en: He said: “Cursed is Canaan; a slave serving slaves shall he be to his brothers.”
meaningNotes: The curse is confined to the named Canaan in this account; it is not a racial classification or practical authorization of slavery.
displayMeaningNotes: The curse is confined to the named Canaan in this account; it is not a racial classification or practical authorization of slavery.

units.he: וַאֲמַר בְּרִיךְ יְיָ אֱלָהֵהּ דְּשֵׁם וִיהֵי כְנַעַן עַבְדָא לְהוֹן:
units.en: He said: “Blessed is the LORD, the God of Shem; let Canaan be their slave.

units.he: יַפְתֵּי יְיָ לְיֶפֶת וְיַשְׁרֵי שְׁכִינְתֵּיהּ בְּמַשְׁכְּנֵיהּ דְּשֵׁם וִיהֵי כְנַעַן עַבְדָא לְהוֹן:
units.en: May the LORD enlarge Yefes, and cause His Divine Presence to dwell in Shem’s dwelling; let Canaan be their slave.”
meaningNotes: The Targum explicitly makes the Divine Presence dwell in Shem’s dwelling.
displayMeaningNotes: The Targum explicitly makes the Divine Presence dwell in Shem’s dwelling.

units.he: וַחֲיָא נֹחַ בָּתַר טוֹפָנָא תְּלַת מְאָה וְחַמְשִׁין שְׁנִין:
units.en: Noach lived for three hundred and fifty years after the flood.

units.he: וַהֲווֹ כָל יוֹמֵי נֹחַ תְּשַׁע מְאָה וְחַמְשִׁין שְׁנִין וּמִית:
units.en: Noach’s days were altogether nine hundred and fifty years, and he died.

units.he: וְאִלֵּין תּוּלְדַת בְּנֵי נֹחַ שֵׁם חָם וָיָפֶת וְאִתְיְלִידוּ לְהוֹן בְּנִין בָּתַר טוֹפָנָא:
units.en: These are the generations of Noach’s sons, Shem, Cham, and Yefes. Children were born to them after the flood.

units.he: בְּנֵי יֶפֶת גּוֹמֶר וּמָגוֹג וּמָדַי וְיָוָן וְתוּבָל וּמֶשֶׁךְ וְתִירָס:
units.en: Yefes’s sons: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Yavan, Tuval, Meshech, and Tiras.

units.he: וּבְנֵי גּוֹמֶר אַשְׁכְּנַז וְרִיפַת וְתוֹגַרְמָה:
units.en: Gomer’s sons: Ashkenaz, Rifas, and Togarmuh.

units.he: וּבְנֵי יָוָן אֶלִישָׁה וְתַרְשִׁישׁ כִּתִּים וְדֹדָנִים:
units.en: Yavan’s sons: Elishuh, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.

units.he: מֵאִלֵּין אִתַּפְרָשׁוּ נַגְוַת עַמְמַיָּא בְּאַרְעֲהוֹן גְּבַר לְלִישָׁנֵיהּ לְזַרְעֲיָתְהוֹן בְּעַמְמֵיהוֹן:
units.en: From these the coastland peoples became separated in their lands, each by its language, by their family lineages, among their peoples.

units.he: וּבְנֵי חָם כּוּשׁ וּמִצְרַיִם וּפוּט וּכְנָעַן:
units.en: Cham’s sons: Cush, Mitzrayim, Put, and Canaan.

units.he: וּבְנֵי כוּשׁ סְבָא וַחֲוִילָה וְסַבְתָּה וְרַעְמָה וְסַבְתְּכָא וּבְנֵי רַעְמָה שְׁבָא וּדְדָן:
units.en: Cush’s sons: Seva, Chaviluh, Savtuh, Raamuh, and Savtecha. Raamuh’s sons: Sheva and Dedan.

units.he: וְכוּשׁ אוֹלִיד יָת נִמְרֹד הוּא שָׁרֵי לְמֵהֲוֵי גִבַּר תַּקִּיף בְּאַרְעָא:
units.en: Cush begot Nimrod; he began to be a mighty, powerful man in the earth.

units.he: הוּא הֲוָה גִבַּר תַּקִּיף קֳדָם יְיָ עַל כֵּן יִתְאֲמַר כְּנִמְרֹד גִּבַּר תַּקִּיף קֳדָם יְיָ:
units.en: He was a mighty, powerful man before the LORD. Therefore people say, “Like Nimrod, a mighty, powerful man before the LORD.”
meaningNotes: The Targum says “mighty, powerful,” not “hunter.”
displayMeaningNotes: The Targum says “mighty, powerful,” not “hunter.”

units.he: וַהֲוָה רֵישׁ מַלְכוּתֵיהּ בָּבֶל וְאֶרֶךְ וְאַכַּד וְכַלְנֵה בְּאַרְעָא דְבָבֶל:
units.en: The beginning of his kingdom consisted of Babel, Erech, Akkad, and Calneh, in the land of Babel.

units.he: מִן אַרְעָא (נ"א עֵיצָה) הַהִיא נְפַק אֲתוּרָאָה וּבְנָא יָת נִינְוֵה וְיָת רְחֹבֹת (נ"א רְחוֹבֵי) קַרְתָּא וְיָת כָּלַח:
units.en: From that land [alternate reading: counsel] the Assyrian went out and built Nineveh, Rechovos Ir [alternate reading: the city’s streets], and Calach,
meaningNotes: The source contains two explicit alternate readings: “counsel” for “land,” and “the city’s streets” for Rechovos Ir. Both remain visible without combining them into one uncontested reading.
displayMeaningNotes: The source contains two explicit alternate readings: “counsel” for “land,” and “the city’s streets” for Rechovos Ir. These are alternatives, not one uncontested reading.

units.he: וְיָת רֶסֶן בֵּין נִינְוֵה וּבֵין כָּלַח הִיא קַרְתָּא רַבְּתָא:
units.en: and Resen, between Nineveh and Calach; it is the great city.
meaningNotes: The source does not expressly identify the antecedent of “the great city.”
displayMeaningNotes: The source does not expressly identify the antecedent of “the great city.”

units.he: וּמִצְרָאֵי (<small>נ"א</small> וּמִצְרַיִם) אוֹלִיד יָת לוּדָאֵי וְיָת עֲנָמָאֵי וְיָת לְהָבָאֵי וְיָת נַפְתּוּחָאֵי:
units.en: Mitzraai [alternate reading: Mitzrayim] begot the Ludites, Anamites, Lehavites, and Naftuchites,
meaningNotes: Both printed name forms are retained; Mitzraai is the Aramaic form associated with Egypt.
displayMeaningNotes: There are two printed name forms here; Mitzraai is the Aramaic form associated with Egypt.

units.he: וְיָת פַּתְרוּסָאֵי וְיָת כַּסְלוּחָאֵי דִּי נְפָקוּ מִתַּמָּן פְּלִשְׁתָּאֵי וְיָת קַפּוּטְקָאֵי:
units.en: and the Patrusites, and the Casluchites, from whom the Philistines came out, and the Cappadocians.
meaningNotes: The Targum identifies this people as the Cappadocians.
displayMeaningNotes: The Targum identifies this people as the Cappadocians.

units.he: וּכְנַעַן אוֹלִיד יָת צִידוֹן בָּכְרֵיהּ וְיָת חֵת:
units.en: Canaan begot Tzidon, his firstborn, and Ches,

units.he: וְיָת יְבוּסָאֵי וְיָת אֱמוֹרָאֵי וְיָת גִּרְגָּשָׁאֵי:
units.en: and the Jebusites, the Amorites, and the Girgashites,

units.he: וְיָת חִוָּאֵי וְיָת עַרְקָאֵי וְיָת אַנְתּוֹסָאֵי:
units.en: and the Hivites, the Arkites, and the Antosites,
meaningNotes: Antosites retains the Targum’s own people-name; its precise historical identification is uncertain.
displayMeaningNotes: Antosites is the Targum’s own people-name; its precise historical identification is uncertain.

units.he: וְיָת אַרְוָדָאֵי וְיָת צְמָרָאֵי וְיָת חֲמָתָאֵי וּבָתַר כֵּן אִתְבַּדָּרוּ זַרְעֲיַת כְּנַעֲנָאֵי:
units.en: and the Arvadites, the Tzemarites, and the Chamasites; afterward the Canaanite family lineages dispersed.

units.he: וַהֲוָה תְּחוּם כְּנַעֲנָאֵי מִצִּידוֹן מָטֵי לִגְרָר עַד עַזָּה מָטֵי לִסְדוֹם וַעֲמוֹרָה וְאַדְמָה וּצְבוֹיִם עַד לָשַׁע:
units.en: The territory of the Canaanites ran from Tzidon, reaching Gerar as far as Azzuh, and reaching Sedom, Amoruh, Admuh, and Tzevoyim as far as Lashuh.

units.he: אִלֵּין בְּנֵי חָם לְזַרְעֲיָתְהוֹן לְלִישָׁנְהוֹן בְּאַרְעָתְהוֹן בְּעַמְמֵיהוֹן:
units.en: These are Cham’s sons, by their family lineages and languages, in their lands and among their peoples.

units.he: וּלְשֵׁם אִתְיְלִיד אַף הוּא אֲבוּהוֹן דְּכָל בְּנֵי עֵבֶר אֲחוּהִי דְּיֶפֶת רַבָּא:
units.en: Children were born to Shem also; he was the father of all Ever’s children, the brother of Yefes the elder.
meaningNotes: The placement of “elder” permits another understanding: Shem as the elder brother of Yefes.
displayMeaningNotes: The placement of “elder” permits another understanding: Shem as the elder brother of Yefes.

units.he: בְּנֵי שֵׁם עֵילָם וְאַשּׁוּר וְאַרְפַּכְשַׁד וְלוּד וַאֲרָם:
units.en: Shem’s sons: Elam, Ashur, Arpachshad, Lud, and Aram.

units.he: וּבְנֵי אֲרָם עוּץ וְחוּל וְגֶתֶר וָמַשׁ:
units.en: Aram’s sons: Utz, Chul, Geser, and Mash.

units.he: וְאַרְפַּכְשַׁד אוֹלִיד יָת שָׁלַח וְשֶׁלַח אוֹלִיד יָת עֵבֶר:
units.en: Arpachshad begot Shelach, and Shelach begot Ever.

units.he: וּלְעֵבֶר אִתְיְלִידוּ תְּרֵין בְּנִין שׁוּם חַד פֶּלֶג אֲרֵי בְּיוֹמוֹהִי אִתְפְּלִיגַת אַרְעָא וְשׁוּם אֲחוּהִי יָקְטָן:
units.en: Two sons were born to Ever. One’s name was Peleg, because in his days the earth was divided; his brother’s name was Yoktan.

units.he: וְיָקְטָן אוֹלִיד יָת אַלְמוֹדָד וְיָת שָׁלֶף וְיָת חֲצַרְמָוֶת וְיָת יָרַח:
units.en: Yoktan begot Almodad, Shalef, Chatzarmaves, and Yerach,

units.he: וְיָת הֲדוֹרָם וְיָת אוּזָל וְיָת דִּקְלָה:
units.en: and Hadoram, Uzal, and Diklah,

units.he: וְיָת עוֹבָל וְיָת אֲבִימָאֵל וְיָת שְׁבָא:
units.en: and Oval, Avimael, and Sheva,

units.he: וְיָת אוֹפִר וְיָת חֲוִילָה וְיָת יוֹבָב כָּל אִלֵּין בְּנֵי יָקְטָן:
units.en: and Ofir, Chaviluh, and Yovav. All these were Yoktan’s sons.

units.he: וַהֲוָה מוֹתְבָנְהוֹן מִמֵּשָׁא מָטֵי לִסְפַר טוּר מָדִינְחָא:
units.en: Their settlement extended from Maishuh, reaching Sefar, the eastern mountain.

units.he: אִלֵּין בְּנֵי שֵׁם לְזַרְעֲיָתְהוֹן לְלִישָׁנְהוֹן לְאַרְעָתְהוֹן בְּעַמְמֵיהוֹן:
units.en: These are Shem’s sons, by their family lineages and languages, according to their lands, among their peoples.

units.he: אִלֵּין זַרְעֲיַת בְּנֵי נֹחַ לְתוּלְדָתְהוֹן בְּעַמְמֵיהוֹן וּמֵאִלֵּין אִתַּפְרָשׁוּ עַמְמַיָּא בְּאַרְעָא בָּתַר טוֹפָנָא:
units.en: These are the family lineages of Noach’s sons, by their generations, among their peoples. From these the peoples became separated in the earth after the flood.

units.he: וַהֲוָה כָל אַרְעָא לִישָׁן חָד וּמַמְלַל חָד:
units.en: The whole earth had one language and one manner of speech.

units.he: וַהֲוָה בְּמִטַּלְהוֹן בְּקַדְמֵיתָא וְאַשְׁכָּחוּ בִּקְעֲתָא בְּאַרְעָא דְבָבֶל וִיתִיבוּ תַמָּן:
units.en: When they traveled at first, they found a plain in the land of Babel and dwelt there.

units.he: וַאֲמָרוּ גְּבַר לְחַבְרֵיהּ הָבוּ נִרְמֵי לִבְנִין וְנִשְׂרְפִנּוּן בְּנוּרָא (יוֹקַדְתָּא) וַהֲוַת לְהוֹן לְבִנְתָּא לְאַבְנָא וְחֵימָרָא הֲוָה לְהוֹן לְשִׁיעַ:
units.en: They said to one another, “Come, let us cast bricks and burn them in fire [burning fire].” The bricks served them as stone, and bitumen served them as plaster.
meaningNotes: The parenthetical “burning fire” is also translated; it does not introduce a second building step.
displayMeaningNotes: The parenthetical “burning fire” is also translated; it does not introduce a second building step.

units.he: וַאֲמָרוּ הָבוּ נִבְנֵי לָנָא קַרְתָּא וּמַגְדְּלָא וְרֵישֵׁיהּ מָטֵי עַד צֵית שְׁמַיָּא וְנַעְבֵּיד לָנָא שׁוּם דִּילְמָא נִתְבַּדַּר עַל אַפֵּי כָל אַרְעָא:
units.en: They said: “Come, let us build ourselves a city and a tower whose top reaches to the height of the heavens. Let us make ourselves a name, lest we be dispersed over the face of the whole earth.”

units.he: וְאִתְגְּלִי יְיָ לְאִתְפְּרָעָא עַל עוֹבָדֵי קַרְתָּא וּמַגְדְּלָא דִּי בְנוֹ בְּנֵי אֱנָשָׁא:
units.en: The LORD revealed Himself to exact punishment for the works of the city and the tower that human beings had built.

units.he: וַאֲמַר יְיָ הָא עַמָּא חַד וְלִישָׁן חַד לְכָלְּהוֹן וְדֵין דְּשָׁרִיוּ לְמֶעְבָּד וּכְעַן לָא יִתִּמְנַע מִנְהוֹן כֹּל דִּחַשִּׁיבוּ לְמֶעְבָּד:
units.en: The LORD said: “They are one people, and all have one language, and this is what they have begun to do. Now nothing they have planned to do will be prevented for them.

units.he: הָבוּ נִתְגְּלִי וּנְבַלְבֵּל תַּמָּן לִישָׁנְהוֹן דִּלָא יִשְׁמְעוּן אֱנַשׁ (גְּבַר) לִישַׁן חַבְרֵיהּ:
units.en: Come, let us reveal ourselves and confuse their language there, so that no person [man] will understand the language of his fellow.”
meaningNotes: The source’s plural Divine speech is retained, without supplying a named group of speakers. The parenthetical “man” is a wording alternative to “person.”
displayMeaningNotes: The Divine speech is plural and does not name a group of speakers. The parenthetical “man” is a wording alternative to “person.”

units.he: וּבַדַּר יְיָ יָתְהוֹן מִתַּמָּן עַל אַפֵּי כָל אַרְעָא וּמְנָעוּ לְמִבְנֵי (<small>נ"י</small> וְאִתְמְנָעוּ מִלְּמִבְנֵי) קַרְתָּא:
units.en: The LORD dispersed them from there over the face of the whole earth, and they ceased building [alternate reading: were prevented from building] the city.
meaningNotes: The parenthetical alternative is preserved separately, rather than silently choosing it over the main wording.
displayMeaningNotes: The parenthetical wording is an alternative to the main wording, not a replacement for it.

units.he: עַל כֵּן קְרָא שְׁמַהּ בָּבֶל אֲרֵי תַמָּן בַּלְבֵּל יְיָ לִישַׁן כָּל אַרְעָא וּמִתַּמָּן בַּדָּרִנּוּן יְיָ עַל אַפֵּי כָּל אַרְעָא:
units.en: Therefore its name was called Babel, for there the LORD confused the language of the whole earth; from there the LORD dispersed them over the face of the whole earth.

units.he: אִלֵּין תּוּלְדַת שֵׁם שֵׁם בַּר מְאָה שְׁנִין וְאוֹלִיד יָת אַרְפַּכְשָׁד תַּרְתֵּין שְׁנִין בָּתַר טוֹפָנָא:
units.en: These are Shem’s generations. Shem was one hundred years old and begot Arpachshad two years after the flood.

units.he: וַחֲיָא שֵׁם בָּתַר דְּאוֹלִיד יָת אַרְפַּכְשָׁד חֲמֵשׁ מְאָה שְׁנִין וְאוֹלִיד בְּנִין וּבְנָן:
units.en: After he begot Arpachshad, Shem lived five hundred years and begot sons and daughters.

units.he: וְאַרְפַּכְשַׁד חֲיָא תְּלָתִין וַחֲמֵשׁ שְׁנִין וְאוֹלִיד יָת שָׁלַח:
units.en: Arpachshad lived thirty-five years and begot Shelach.

units.he: וַחֲיָא אַרְפַּכְשַׁד בָּתַר דְּאוֹלִיד יָת שֶׁלַח אַרְבַּע מְאָה וּתְלָת שְׁנִין וְאוֹלִיד בְּנִין וּבְנָן:
units.en: After he begot Shelach, Arpachshad lived four hundred and three years and begot sons and daughters.

units.he: וְשֶׁלַח חֲיָא תְּלָתִין שְׁנִין וְאוֹלִיד יָת עֵבֶר:
units.en: Shelach lived thirty years and begot Ever.

units.he: וַחֲיָא שֶׁלַח בָּתַר דְּאוֹלִיד יָת עֵבֶר אַרְבַּע מְאָה וּתְלָת שְׁנִין וְאוֹלִיד בְּנִין וּבְנָן:
units.en: After he begot Ever, Shelach lived four hundred and three years and begot sons and daughters.

units.he: וַחֲיָא עֵבֶר תְּלָתִין וְאַרְבַּע שְׁנִין וְאוֹלִיד יָת פָּלֶג:
units.en: Ever lived thirty-four years and begot Peleg.

units.he: וַחֲיָא עֵבֶר בָּתַר דְּאוֹלִיד יָת פֶּלֶג אַרְבַּע מְאָה וּתְלָתִין שְׁנִין וְאוֹלִיד בְּנִין וּבְנָן:
units.en: After he begot Peleg, Ever lived four hundred and thirty years and begot sons and daughters.

units.he: וַחֲיָא פֶלֶג תְּלָתִין שְׁנִין וְאוֹלִיד יָת רְעוּ:
units.en: Peleg lived thirty years and begot Reu.

units.he: וַחֲיָא פֶלֶג בָּתַר דְּאוֹלִיד יָת רְעוּ מָאתָן וּתְשַׁע שְׁנִין וְאוֹלִיד בְּנִין וּבְנָן:
units.en: After he begot Reu, Peleg lived two hundred and nine years and begot sons and daughters.

units.he: וַחֲיָא רְעוּ תְּלָתִין וְתַרְתֵּין שְׁנִין וְאוֹלִיד יָת שְׂרוּג:
units.en: Reu lived thirty-two years and begot Serug.

units.he: וַחֲיָא רְעוּ בָּתַר דְּאוֹלִיד יָת שְׂרוּג מָאתָן וּשְׁבַע שְׁנִין וְאוֹלִיד בְּנִין וּבְנָן:
units.en: After he begot Serug, Reu lived two hundred and seven years and begot sons and daughters.

units.he: וַחֲיָא שְׂרוּג תְּלָתִין שְׁנִין וְאוֹלִיד יָת נָחוֹר:
units.en: Serug lived thirty years and begot Nachor.

units.he: וַחֲיָא שְׂרוּג בָּתַר דְּאוֹלִיד יָת נָחוֹר מָאתָן שְׁנִין וְאוֹלִיד בְּנִין וּבְנָן:
units.en: After he begot Nachor, Serug lived two hundred years and begot sons and daughters.

units.he: וַחֲיָא נָחוֹר עֶשְׂרִין וּתְשַׁע שְׁנִין וְאוֹלִיד יָת תָּרַח:
units.en: Nachor lived twenty-nine years and begot Terach.

units.he: וַחֲיָא נָחוֹר בָּתַר דְּאוֹלִיד יָת תֶּרַח מְאָה וּתְשַׁע עֲשַׂר שְׁנִין וְאוֹלִיד בְּנִין וּבְנָן:
units.en: After he begot Terach, Nachor lived one hundred and nineteen years and begot sons and daughters.

units.he: וַחֲיָא תֶרַח שִׁבְעִין שְׁנִין וְאוֹלִיד יָת אַבְרָם יָת נָחוֹר וְיָת הָרָן:
units.en: Terach lived seventy years and begot Avram, Nachor, and Haran.

units.he: וְאִלֵּין תּוּלְדַת תֶּרַח תֶּרַח אוֹלִיד יָת אַבְרָם יָת נָחוֹר וְיָת הָרָן וְהָרָן אוֹלִיד יָת לוֹט:
units.en: These are Terach’s generations: Terach begot Avram, Nachor, and Haran; Haran begot Lot.

units.he: וּמִית הָרָן עַל אַפֵּי תֶּרַח אֲבוּהִי בְּאַרְעָא דְיַלָּדוּתֵיהּ בְּאוּרָא דְכַסְדָּאֵי:
units.en: Haran died in the presence of Terach his father, in the land where he was born, in Ur [or: the fire] of the Chaldeans.
meaningNotes: The Aramaic אוּרָא is rendered here as “fire.” It also corresponds to the place-name Ur in the parallel biblical account; the wording alone does not establish an additional statement about the cause of Haran’s death.
displayMeaningNotes: אוּרָא can be read as the place-name Ur or as “the fire.” The geographical context supports Ur, but this wording does not by itself settle the alternative or say how Haran died.

units.he: וּנְסִיב אַבְרָם וְנָחוֹר לְהוֹן נְשִׁין שׁוּם אִתַּת אַבְרָם שָׂרָי וְשׁוּם אִתַּת נָחוֹר מִלְכָּה בַּת הָרָן אֲבוּהָא דְמִלְכָּה וַאֲבוּהָא דְיִסְכָּה:
units.en: Avram and Nachor took wives. Avram’s wife was named Sarai; Nachor’s wife was named Milkah, the daughter of Haran, who was Milkah’s father and Yiskuh’s father.

units.he: וַהֲוַת שָׂרַי עֲקָרָה לֵית לָהּ וְלָד:
units.en: Sarai was barren; she had no offspring.

units.he: וּדְבַר תֶּרַח יָת אַבְרָם בְּרֵיהּ וְיָת לוֹט בַּר הָרָן בַּר בְּרֵיהּ וְיָת שָׂרַי כַּלָּתֵיהּ אִתַּת אַבְרָם בְּרֵיהּ וּנְפָקוּ עִמְּהוֹן מֵאוּרָא דְכַסְדָּאֵי לְמֵיזַל לְאַרְעָא דִכְנָעַן וַאֲתוֹ עַד חָרָן וִיתִיבוּ תַמָּן:
units.en: Terach led Avram his son, Lot son of Haran, his grandson, and Sarai his daughter-in-law, Avram his son’s wife. They came out with them from Ur [or: the fire] of the Chaldeans to go to Canaan’s land. They reached Charan and dwelt there.
meaningNotes: The Aramaic אוּרָא is again rendered here as “fire”; it corresponds to Ur in the parallel biblical account, so its use as a place-name remains a possible reading. The Targum says that Terach “led” the family.
displayMeaningNotes: אוּרָא again allows Ur or “the fire.” Leaving it, travelling toward Canaan, and settling at Charan make the geographical reading natural, without excluding the literal alternative. The Targum says Terach “led” the family; The referent of “with them” is not explicit.

units.he: וַהֲווֹ יוֹמֵי תֶרַח מָאתָן וַחֲמֵשׁ שְׁנִין וּמִית תֶּרַח בְּחָרָן:
units.en: Terach’s days were two hundred and five years, and Terach died in Charan.

units.he: הַטָּמֵא שֶׁיָּרַד לִטְבֹּל, סָפֵק טָבַל סָפֵק לֹא טָבַל, אֲפִלּוּ טָבַל, סָפֵק יֶשׁ בּוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה סָפֵק אֵין בּוֹ. שְׁנֵי מִקְוָאוֹת, אֶחָד יֶשׁ בּוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה וְאֶחָד שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ, טָבַל בְּאַחַד מֵהֶם וְאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ בְּאֵיזֶה מֵהֶן טָבַל, סְפֵקוֹ טָמֵא:
units.en: An impure person went down to immerse, but it is uncertain whether he immersed or did not immerse. Even if he immersed, it is uncertain whether the pool contained forty se’uh or did not contain them. [Or] there were two immersion pools, one containing forty se’uh and one not containing them, and he immersed in one but does not know in which he immersed. In these doubtful cases, he is impure.
meaningNotes: Se’uh and log are the source’s volume measures. The cases are alternatives, not a sequence in which one person passes through every pool.
displayMeaningNotes: Se’uh and log are the source’s volume measures. The cases are alternatives, not a sequence in which one person passes through every pool.

units.he: מִקְוֶה שֶׁנִּמְדַּד וְנִמְצָא חָסֵר, כָּל טָהֳרוֹת שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ עַל גַּבָּיו לְמַפְרֵעַ, בֵּין בִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד בֵּין בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים, טְמֵאוֹת. בַּמֶּה דְבָרִים אֲמוּרִים, בְּטֻמְאָה חֲמוּרָה. אֲבָל בְּטֻמְאָה קַלָּה, כְּגוֹן אָכַל אֳכָלִים טְמֵאִים, וְשָׁתָה מַשְׁקִין טְמֵאִים, בָּא רֹאשׁוֹ וְרֻבּוֹ בְּמַיִם שְׁאוּבִים, אוֹ שֶׁנָּפְלוּ עַל רֹאשׁוֹ וְעַל רֻבּוֹ שְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין מַיִם שְׁאוּבִין, וְיָרַד לִטְבֹּל, סָפֵק טָבַל סָפֵק לֹא טָבַל, אֲפִלּוּ טָבַל, סָפֵק יֶשׁ בּוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה סָפֵק אֵין בּוֹ. שְׁנֵי מִקְוָאוֹת, אֶחָד יֶשׁ בּוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה, וְאֶחָד שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ, טָבַל בְּאַחַד מֵהֶן וְאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ בְּאֵיזֶה מֵהֶן טָבַל, סְפֵקוֹ טָהוֹר. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מְטַמֵּא, שֶׁרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, כָּל דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא בְחֶזְקַת טֻמְאָה, לְעוֹלָם הוּא בִפְסוּלוֹ, עַד שֶׁיִּוָּדַע שֶׁטָּהַר. אֲבָל סְפֵקוֹ לִטָּמֵא וּלְטַמֵּא, טָהוֹר:
units.en: If an immersion pool was measured and found deficient, all things treated as pure by means of it retrospectively are impure, whether in a private domain or a public domain. When does this apply? In a case of severe impurity. But with lighter impurity—for example, someone ate impure food, drank impure liquids, put his head and most of his body into drawn water, or had three log of drawn water fall on his head and most of his body—and he went down to immerse, but it is uncertain whether he immersed or did not immerse; even if he immersed, it is uncertain whether the pool contained forty se’uh or did not; or there were two immersion pools, one containing forty se’uh and one not containing them, and he immersed in one but does not know in which—in these doubtful cases, he is pure. Rabbi Yose declares him impure, for Rabbi Yose says: Anything with an established presumption of impurity always remains disqualified until it is known to have become pure. But if the doubt concerns whether it became impure or imparted impurity, it is pure.
meaningNotes: Severe and lighter impurity have separate treatments. Rabbi Yose’s established-impurity rule is distinct from a doubt about whether impurity arose at all.
displayMeaningNotes: Severe and lighter impurity have separate treatments. Rabbi Yose’s established-impurity rule is distinct from a doubt about whether impurity arose at all.

units.he: סְפֵק מַיִם שְׁאוּבִין שֶׁטִּהֲרוּ חֲכָמִים, סָפֵק נָפְלוּ, סָפֵק לֹא נָפְלוּ, אֲפִלּוּ נָפְלוּ, סָפֵק יֶשׁ בָּהֶם אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה סָפֵק אֵין בָּהֶם, שְׁנֵי מִקְוָאוֹת, אֶחָד יֶשׁ בּוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה וְאֶחָד אֵין בּוֹ, נָפַל לְאַחַד מֵהֶן וְאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ לְאֵיזֶה מֵהֶן נָפַל, סְפֵקוֹ טָהוֹר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ בַמֶּה יִתְלֶה. הָיוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם פְּחוּתִים מֵאַרְבָּעִים סְאָה, וְנָפַל לְאַחַד מֵהֶם וְאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ לְאֵיזֶה מֵהֶן נָפַל, סְפֵקוֹ טָמֵא, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ בַמֶּה יִתְלֶה:
units.en: The doubtful drawn-water cases that the Sages declared pure are these: It is uncertain whether [drawn water] fell in or did not fall in; even if it fell in, it is uncertain whether [the pool] contained forty se’uh or did not contain them; or there were two immersion pools, one containing forty se’uh and one not containing them, and it fell into one but it is not known into which. Its doubtful status is pure, because there is a basis on which to attribute [the fall permissibly]. If both contained less than forty se’uh, and it fell into one but it is not known into which, its doubtful status is impure, because there is no basis on which to attribute [the fall permissibly].
meaningNotes: The doubtful “forty se’uh” concerns the pool’s valid water, not a requirement that the fallen drawn water itself measure forty se’uh. A complete pool and an incomplete pool have different drawn-water consequences.
displayMeaningNotes: The doubtful “forty se’uh” concerns the pool’s valid water, not a requirement that the fallen drawn water itself measure forty se’uh. A complete pool and an incomplete pool have different drawn-water consequences.

units.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, רְבִיעִית מַיִם שְׁאוּבִין בַּתְּחִלָּה, פּוֹסְלִין אֶת הַמִּקְוֶה, וּשְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין עַל פְּנֵי הַמַּיִם. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, בֵּין בַּתְּחִלָּה בֵּין בַּסּוֹף, שִׁעוּרוֹ שְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין:
units.en: Rabbi Eliezer says: A quarter-log of drawn water at the beginning invalidates an immersion pool, and three log [invalidate it when falling] upon water already present. The Sages say: Whether at the beginning or at the end, the measure is three log.

units.he: מִקְוֶה שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ שָׁלשׁ גֻּמּוֹת שֶׁל מַיִם שְׁאוּבִין שֶׁל לֹג לֹג, אִם יָדוּעַ שֶׁנָּפַל לְתוֹכוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאִין מַיִם כְּשֵׁרִין עַד שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעוּ לַגֻּמָּא הַשְּׁלִישִׁית, כָּשֵׁר. וְאִם לָאו, פָּסוּל. וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַכְשִׁיר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא כְמִקְוֶה סָמוּךְ לְמִקְוֶה:
units.en: An immersion pool contains three hollows of drawn water, each of one log. If it is known that forty se’uh of valid water fell into it before [that water] reached the third hollow, it is valid; if not, it is invalid. Rabbi Shimon declares it valid, because it is like an immersion pool alongside an immersion pool.

units.he: הַמְסַנֵּק אֶת הַטִּיט לַצְּדָדִין וּמָשְׁכוּ מִמֶּנּוּ שְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין, כָּשֵׁר. הָיָה תוֹלֵשׁ וּמָשְׁכוּ מִמֶּנּוּ שְׁלשָׁה לֻגִּין, פָּסוּל. וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַכְשִׁיר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁלֹּא נִתְכַּוֵּן לִשְׁאֹב:
units.en: If someone pushes the mud to the sides and three log [of water] flow from it, [the pool] is valid. If he was lifting the mud out and three log flowed from it, it is invalid. Rabbi Shimon declares it valid, because he did not intend to draw water.
meaningNotes: Pushing mud aside and removing it are alternative actions, with Rabbi Shimon dissenting in the second case.
displayMeaningNotes: Pushing mud aside and removing it are alternative actions, with Rabbi Shimon dissenting in the second case.

units.he: הַמַּנִּיחַ קַנְקַנִּים בְּרֹאשׁ הַגַּג לְנַגְּבָן וְנִתְמַלְּאוּ מַיִם, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, אִם עוֹנַת גְּשָׁמִים הִיא, אִם יֶשׁ בּוֹ כִמְעַט מַיִם בַּבּוֹר, יְשַׁבֵּר. וְאִם לָאו, לֹא יְשַׁבֵּר. רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ יְשַׁבֵּר, אוֹ יִכְפֶּה, אֲבָל לֹא יְעָרֶה:
units.en: If someone places jars on the roof to dry them and they fill with water, Rabbi Eliezer says: If it is the rainy season, and there is a little water in the cistern, he may break them; if not, he may not break them. Rabbi Yehoshua says: In either case, he may break them or overturn them, but he may not pour them out.
meaningNotes: Breaking or overturning the jars is distinguished from pouring their water; the rainy-season and existing-water conditions are retained.
displayMeaningNotes: Breaking or overturning the jars is distinguished from pouring their water; the cases depend on the rainy season and the presence of water already in the pool.

units.he: הַסַּיָּד שֶׁשָּׁכַח עָצִיץ בַּבּוֹר וְנִתְמַלֵּא מַיִם, אִם הָיוּ הַמַּיִם צָפִים עַל גַּבָּיו כָּל שֶׁהוּא, יְשַׁבֵּר. וְאִם לָאו, לֹא יְשַׁבֵּר, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר. וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ יְשַׁבֵּר:
units.en: If a plasterer forgot a pot in the cistern and it filled with water, then if water floats over its top to any extent, he may break it; if not, he may not break it. These are the words of Rabbi Eliezer. Rabbi Yehoshua says: In either case, he may break it.

units.he: הַמְסַדֵּר קַנְקַנִּים בְּתוֹךְ הַבּוֹר וְנִתְמַלְּאוּ מַיִם, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁבָּלַע הַבּוֹר אֶת מֵימָיו, הֲרֵי זֶה יְשַׁבֵּר:
units.en: If someone arranged jars within the cistern and they filled with water, even if the cistern absorbed its water, he may break them.

units.he: מִקְוֶה שֶׁיֶּשׁ בּוֹ אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה מַיִם וָטִיט, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, מַטְבִּילִין בַּמַּיִם וְאֵין מַטְבִּילִין בַּטִּיט. רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, בַּמַּיִם וּבַטִּיט. בְּאֵיזֶה טִיט מַטְבִּילִין. בְּטִיט שֶׁהַמַּיִם צָפִים עַל גַּבָּיו. הָיוּ הַמַּיִם מִצַּד אֶחָד, מוֹדֶה רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ שֶׁמַּטְבִּילִין בַּמַּיִם וְאֵין מַטְבִּילִין בַּטִּיט. בְּאֵיזֶה טִיט אָמְרוּ. בְּטִיט שֶׁהַקָּנֶה יוֹרֵד מֵאֵלָיו, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, מְקוֹם שֶׁאֵין קְנֵה הַמִּדָּה עוֹמֵד. אַבָּא אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן דּוֹלְעַאי אוֹמֵר, מְקוֹם שֶׁהַמִּשְׁקֹלֶת יוֹרֶדֶת. רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, הַיּוֹרֵד בְּפִי חָבִית. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, הַנִּכְנָס בִּשְׁפוֹפֶרֶת הַנּוֹד. רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר צָדוֹק אוֹמֵר, הַנִּמְדָּד בַּלֹּג:
units.en: An immersion pool contains forty se’uh of water and mud. Rabbi Eliezer says: One may immerse in the water but not in the mud. Rabbi Yehoshua says: In the water and in the mud. In what mud may one immerse? Mud with water floating over it. If the water is on one side, Rabbi Yehoshua agrees that one may immerse in the water but not in the mud. Of what kind of mud did they speak? Mud into which a reed sinks by itself; these are the words of Rabbi Meir. Rabbi Yehudah says: Where a measuring reed does not stand. Abba Elazar ben Dolai says: Where a plumb weight sinks. Rabbi Eliezer says: [Mud] that passes through the mouth of a barrel. Rabbi Shimon says: [Mud] that enters the neck-tube of a wineskin. Rabbi Elazar bar Tzadok says: [Mud] that can be measured in a log vessel.
meaningNotes: The successive descriptions are alternative tests of sufficiently fluid mud. They do not assert that every type of mud may be used for immersion.
displayMeaningNotes: The successive descriptions are alternative tests of sufficiently fluid mud. They do not assert that every type of mud may be used for immersion.

units.he: מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי, נִתָּן לַאֲכִילָה וְלִשְׁתִיָּה וּלְסִיכָה, לֶאֱכֹל דָּבָר שֶׁדַּרְכּוֹ לֶאֱכֹל, לָסוּךְ דָּבָר שֶׁדַּרְכּוֹ לָסוּךְ. לֹא יָסוּךְ יַיִן וְחֹמֶץ, אֲבָל סָךְ הוּא אֶת הַשֶּׁמֶן. אֵין מְפַטְּמִין שֶׁמֶן שֶׁל מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי, וְאֵין לוֹקְחִין בִּדְמֵי מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי שֶׁמֶן מְפֻטָּם, אֲבָל מְפַטֵּם הוּא אֶת הַיַּיִן. נָפַל לְתוֹכוֹ דְבַשׁ וּתְבָלִין וְהִשְׁבִּיחוֹ, הַשֶּׁבַח לְפִי חֶשְׁבּוֹן. דָּגִים שֶׁנִּתְבַּשְּׁלוּ עִם הַקַּפְלוֹטוֹת שֶׁל מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי וְהִשְׁבִּיחוּ, הַשֶּׁבַח לְפִי חֶשְׁבּוֹן. עִסָּה שֶׁל מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי שֶׁאֲפָאָהּ וְהִשְׁבִּיחַ, הַשֶּׁבַח לַשֵּׁנִי. זֶה הַכְּלָל, כָּל שֶׁשִּׁבְחוֹ נִכָּר, הַשֶּׁבַח לְפִי הַחֶשְׁבּוֹן. וְכָל שֶׁאֵין שִׁבְחוֹ נִכָּר, הַשֶּׁבַח לַשֵּׁנִי:
units.en: Second tithe is given for eating, drinking, and anointing: to eat what is ordinarily eaten and to anoint with what is ordinarily used for anointing. One may not anoint with wine or vinegar, but may anoint with oil. One may not perfume second-tithe oil or buy perfumed oil with second-tithe money, but one may flavor the wine. If honey and spices fell into it and improved it, the increase in value is apportioned proportionately. If fish were cooked with second-tithe leeks and improved, the increase in value is apportioned proportionately. If second-tithe dough was baked and improved, the increase belongs to the second tithe. This is the rule: Whenever its contribution to the improvement is recognizable, the increase is apportioned proportionately; whenever its contribution is not recognizable, the increase belongs to the second tithe.
meaningNotes: The increase is allocated between the tithe ingredient and ordinary additions according to their contributions; the source distinguishes an identifiable added contribution from improvement such as baking the tithe dough itself.
displayMeaningNotes: The increase is allocated between the tithe ingredient and ordinary additions according to their contributions; the source distinguishes an identifiable added contribution from improvement such as baking the tithe dough itself.

units.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, אֵין סָכִין שֶׁמֶן שֶׁל מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם. וַחֲכָמִים מַתִּירִין. אָמְרוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, אִם הֵקֵל בִּתְרוּמָה חֲמוּרָה, לֹא נָקֵל בְּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי הַקַּל. אָמַר לָהֶם, מַה, לֹא, אִם הֵקֵל בִּתְרוּמָה הַחֲמוּרָה מְקוֹם שֶׁהֵקֵל בְּכַרְשִׁינִים וּבְתִלְתָּן, נָקֵל בְּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי הַקַּל מְקוֹם שֶׁלֹּא הֵקֵל בְּכַרְשִׁינִים וּבְתִלְתָּן:
units.en: Rabbi Shimon says: One may not anoint with second-tithe oil in Jerusalem. The Sages permit it. They said to Rabbi Shimon: If [the law] was lenient with the more stringent heave offering, should we not be lenient with the less stringent second tithe? He said to them: No. If it was lenient with the more stringent heave offering, in a case where it was lenient with vetches and fenugreek, should we be lenient with the less stringent second tithe, in a case where it was not lenient with vetches and fenugreek?

units.he: תִּלְתָּן שֶׁל מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי, תֵּאָכֵל צִמְחוֹנִים. וְשֶׁל תְּרוּמָה, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, כָּל מַעֲשֶׂיהָ בְּטָהֳרָה, חוּץ מֵחֲפִיפָתָהּ. וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, כָּל מַעֲשֶׂיהָ בְטֻמְאָה, חוּץ מִשְּׁרִיָּתָהּ:
units.en: Second-tithe fenugreek must be eaten as young greens. With fenugreek of the heave offering, Bais Shammai say: All its processing must be in purity, except using it to rub the head. Bais Hillel say: All its processing may be in impurity, except soaking it.
meaningNotes: The term צמחונים has an uncertain sense here; it should not be assumed to mean sprouts.
displayMeaningNotes: Bartenura’s classical commentary explains צמחונים as tender, moist greens, before they grow beyond fitness for eating—not specifically germinated sprouts. It explains חפיפה as rubbing the head with fenugreek. The purity requirements distinguish this heave-offering produce; for Bais Hillel, soaking in water is the exception because it makes the produce susceptible to impurity.

units.he: כַּרְשִׁינֵי מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי, יֵאָכְלוּ צִמְחוֹנִים, וְנִכְנָסִין לִירוּשָׁלַיִם וְיוֹצְאִין. נִטְמְאוּ, רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר, יִתְחַלְּקוּ לְעִסּוֹת, וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, יִפָּדוּ. וְשֶׁל תְּרוּמָה, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, שׁוֹרִין וְשָׁפִין בְּטָהֳרָה, וּמַאֲכִילִין בְּטֻמְאָה. וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, שׁוֹרִין בְּטָהֳרָה, וְשָׁפִין וּמַאֲכִילִין בְּטֻמְאָה. שַׁמַּאי אוֹמֵר, יֵאָכְלוּ צָרִיד. רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, כָּל מַעֲשֵׂיהֶן בְּטֻמְאָה:
units.en: Second-tithe vetches must be eaten as young greens, and may be brought into Jerusalem and taken out. If they became impure, Rabbi Tarfon says: They must be divided among doughs; the Sages say: They must be redeemed. With vetches of the heave offering, Bais Shammai say: They are soaked and rubbed in purity, but may be fed in impurity. Bais Hillel say: They are soaked in purity, but may be rubbed and fed in impurity. Shammai says: They must be eaten dry. Rabbi Akiva says: All their processing may be in impurity.
meaningNotes: “Divided among doughs” preserves Rabbi Tarfon’s treatment of the impure vetches, alongside the Sages’ distinct redemption alternative. “Fed” concerns feeding vetches, not an instruction to consume impure sacred produce.
displayMeaningNotes: Bartenura explains צמחונים in the preceding Mishna as young greens; it does not specify germinated sprouts. Bartenura explains “divided among doughs” as putting less than an egg-volume of the impure vetches in each pure second-tithe dough. He explains rubbing as rubbing on the body, feeding as feeding an animal, and צריד as dry. Rabbi Tarfon’s distribution and the Sages’ redemption remain distinct views.

units.he: מְעוֹת חֻלִּין וּמְעוֹת מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי שֶׁנִּתְפַּזְּרוּ, מַה שֶּׁלִּקֵּט, לִקֵּט לְמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי, עַד שֶׁיַּשְׁלִים, וְהַשְּׁאָר חֻלִּין. אִם בָּלַל וְחָפַן, לְפִי חֶשְׁבּוֹן. זֶה הַכְּלָל, הַמִּתְלַקְּטִים, לְמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי. וְהַנִּבְלָלִים, לְפִי חֶשְׁבּוֹן:
units.en: If ordinary coins and second-tithe coins were scattered, whatever one collects is collected for second tithe until he has completed its amount; the remainder is ordinary. If he mixed them and took a handful, [the statuses are assigned] proportionately. This is the rule: Coins collected individually are for second tithe; mixed coins are assigned proportionately.

units.he: סֶלַע שֶׁל מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי וְשֶׁל חֻלִּין שֶׁנִּתְעָרְבוּ, מֵבִיא בְסֶלַע מָעוֹת וְאוֹמֵר, סֶלַע שֶׁל מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי, בְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁהִיא, מְחֻלֶּלֶת עַל הַמָּעוֹת הָאֵלּוּ, וּבוֹרֵר אֶת הַיָּפָה שֶׁבָּהּ, וּמְחַלְּלָן עָלֶיהָ, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאָמְרוּ, מְחַלְּלִין כֶּסֶף עַל נְחֹשֶׁת מִדֹּחַק, וְלֹא שֶׁיִּתְקַיֵּם כֵּן, אֶלָּא חוֹזֵר וּמְחַלְּלָם עַל הַכָּסֶף:
units.en: If a second-tithe sela coin and an ordinary sela coin were mixed, one brings a sela’s worth of small coins and says: “The second-tithe sela, wherever it is, is redeemed onto these coins.” He selects the better [sela] from the mixture and redeems them onto it. For they said: Silver may be redeemed onto copper in a pressing situation, not to remain that way; rather, one afterward redeems them back onto silver.
meaningNotes: A sela and the smaller denominations are monetary measures, not modern amounts. Redemption here transfers second-tithe sanctity between the identified coins.
displayMeaningNotes: A sela and the smaller denominations are monetary measures, not modern amounts. Redemption here transfers second-tithe sanctity between the identified coins.

units.he: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, לֹא יַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם אֶת סְלָעָיו דִּינְרֵי זָהָב, וּבֵית הִלֵּל מַתִּירִין. אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, אֲנִי עָשִׂיתִי לְרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וּלְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אֶת כַּסְפָּן דִּינְרֵי זָהָב:
units.en: Bais Shammai say: A person may not convert his sela coins into gold dinars. Bais Hillel permit it. Rabbi Akiva said: I converted the silver of Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Yehoshua into gold dinars.

units.he: הַפּוֹרֵט סֶלַע מִמְּעוֹת מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, כָּל הַסֶּלַע מָעוֹת. וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, שֶׁקֶל כֶּסֶף וְשֶׁקֶל מָעוֹת. רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, אֵין מְחַלְּלִין כֶּסֶף וּפֵרוֹת עַל הַכֶּסֶף, וַחֲכָמִים מַתִּירִים:
units.en: When converting a sela’s worth of second-tithe small coins [into silver], Bais Shammai say: The entire sela is to be in small coins. Bais Hillel say: A shekel in silver and a shekel in small coins. Rabbi Meir says: One may not redeem silver and produce together onto silver; the Sages permit it.

units.he: הַפּוֹרֵט סֶלַע שֶׁל מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, כָּל הַסֶּלַע מָעוֹת. וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, שֶׁקֶל כֶּסֶף וְשֶׁקֶל מָעוֹת. הַדָּנִין לִפְנֵי חֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה דִינָרֵי כֶּסֶף וְדִינָר מָעוֹת. רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, שְׁלֹשָׁה דִינָרִין כֶּסֶף, וּרְבִיעִית מָעוֹת. רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר, אַרְבָּעָה אַסְפְּרֵי כֶסֶף. שַׁמַּאי אוֹמֵר, יַנִּיחֶנָּה בַחֲנוּת וְיֹאכַל כְּנֶגְדָּהּ:
units.en: If someone makes change for a second-tithe sela in Jerusalem, Bais Shammai say: The entire sela is to be in small coins. Bais Hillel say: A shekel in silver and a shekel in small coins. Those who argue before the Sages say: Three dinars in silver and a dinar in small coins. Rabbi Akiva says: Three dinars in silver, and a quarter [of the fourth dinar] in small coins. Rabbi Tarfon says: Four silver asper coins. Shammai says: Leave it with the shopkeeper and eat against its value.
meaningNotes: Rabbi Akiva’s wording says “a quarter” without explicitly naming its denomination or stating how the remaining value is handled. The fraction should not be treated as an unambiguous quarter of the remaining dinar.
displayMeaningNotes: Bartenura’s classical commentary explains Rabbi Akiva’s “quarter” as a quarter of the fourth dinar: one-sixteenth of the sela in copper small change, with the other three-quarters of that dinar retained in silver. The bracket identifies this supplied denomination; the Mishnah does not itself name it. Bartenura also explains Rabbi Tarfon’s four silver asper coins as accompanied by one copper asper, one-twentieth of the sela. That commentary detail is not additional Mishnah wording.

units.he: מִי שֶׁהָיוּ מִקְצָת בָּנָיו טְמֵאִין וּמִקְצָתָן טְהוֹרִים, מַנִּיחַ אֶת הַסֶּלַע וְאוֹמֵר, מַה שֶּׁהַטְּהוֹרִים שׁוֹתִים, סֶלַע זוֹ מְחֻלֶּלֶת עָלָיו. נִמְצְאוּ טְהוֹרִים וּטְמֵאִים שׁוֹתִין מִכַּד אֶחָד:
units.en: If some of a person’s children were impure and some pure, he places the sela and says: “Whatever the pure ones drink, this sela is redeemed onto it.” Thus the pure and impure ones drink from a single jar.
meaningNotes: The declaration binds tithe sanctity only to what the pure children drink; the shared jar does not make the impure children’s portion second tithe.
displayMeaningNotes: The declaration binds tithe sanctity only to what the pure children drink; the shared jar does not make the impure children’s portion second tithe.

talmud.reference: Niddah 8b:19–21 continuing into 9a; ending הנח מעת לעת דרבנן

units.he: ת״ר הרי שהיתה בחזקת מעוברת וראתה דם ואח״כ הפילה רוח או כל דבר שאינו של קיימא הרי היא בחזקתה ודיה שעתה ואע״פ שאין ראיה לדבר זכר לדבר שנא׳ הרינו חלנו כמו ילדנו רוח מאי זכר לדבר הרי ראיה גדולה היא כי כתיב האי קרא בזכרים כתיב ורמינהי קשתה שנים ולשלישי הפילה רוח או כל דבר שאינו של קיימא הרי זו יולדת בזוב ואי אמרת לידה מעלייתא היא קושי סמוך ללידה רחמנא טהריה אמר רב פפי הנח מעת לעת דרבנן:
units.en: The Rabbis taught: If a woman was presumed pregnant, saw blood, and afterward discharged wind or anything that could not survive, she retains her presumed status, and impurity is reckoned only from the time of her sighting. Although there is no proof for the matter, there is an allusion to the matter, as it is said, ‘We conceived, we writhed; it was as though we gave birth to wind.’ Why call it an allusion? It is a strong proof! Because that verse is written about males. But the following teaching contradicts this: If she experienced labor pains [with bleeding] for two days and on the third discharged wind or anything that could not survive, she is regarded as giving birth while a zavah. If you say that this is a genuine birth, the Torah exempts blood caused by labor pains close to a birth! Rav Pappi said: Set aside [the rule of retrospective impurity for] twenty-four hours, which is rabbinic.
displayMeaningNotes: This ancient passage concerns ritual impurity, not medical diagnosis or treatment. Its presumptions do not establish that a pregnancy or bleeding episode is medically safe; pregnancy complications or bleeding require qualified medical care. The excerpt ends at Rav Pappi’s distinction concerning the rabbinic twenty-four-hour rule and does not contain the following argument.

units.he: העושה מלאכה בערב שבת מן המנחה ולמעלה אינו רואה סימן ברכה יש מפרשים מנחה גדולה ויש מפרשים מנחה קטנה: הגה ודוקא כשעושה מלאכה דרך קבע אבל אם עושה אותה דרך עראי לפי שעה ולא קבע עליה שרי (ב"י בשם א"ז) ולכן מותר לכתוב אגרת שלומים וכל כיוצא בזה (ד"ע):
units.en: One who performs work on the eve of Shabbos from the afternoon time onward does not see a sign of blessing. Some explain this as the earlier afternoon time (מנחה גדולה), and some explain it as the later afternoon time (מנחה קטנה). Gloss: This applies specifically when he performs work as a regular occupation. But if he does it incidentally for a short time and does not make it a regular occupation, it is permitted (ב"י בשם א"ז). Therefore it is permitted to write a letter of greetings and anything similar (ד"ע).
displayMeaningNotes: There are two interpretations of the afternoon threshold: the earlier and later afternoon times. The gloss distinguishes regular occupational work from a brief incidental task. The stated absence of a sign of blessing is not itself a blanket prohibition.

units.he: לתקן בגדיו וכליו לצורך שבת מותר כל היום: הגה וה"ה בגדי חבירו אם הוא לצורך שבת ואינו נוטל עליו שכר ב"י והוא הדין למי שכותב ספרים לעצמו דרך לימודו: הגה אבל אסור לכתוב לחבירו בשכר (מרדכי פ' מקום שנהגו) ומסתפרין כל היום אפי' מספר ישראל (כל בו וב"י) ויש לאדם למעט קצת בלמודו בע"ש כדי שיכין צרכי שבת (ש"ג פי"ו דשבת ירוש' פ"ק דתענית):
units.en: It is permitted to repair his clothes and utensils for Shabbos throughout the day. Gloss: The same applies to his fellow’s clothes if it is for Shabbos and he takes no payment for it (ב"י). The same applies to one who writes books for himself in the course of his study. Gloss: But it is forbidden to write for his fellow for payment (מרדכי פ' מקום שנהגו). One may have a haircut throughout the day, even from a Jewish barber (כל בו וב"י). A person should reduce his study somewhat on the eve of Shabbos so that he can prepare the requirements of Shabbos (ש"ג פי"ו דשבת ירוש' פ"ק דתענית).
displayMeaningNotes: The permissions concern preparation for Shabbos. Repairing another’s clothes here requires Shabbos use and no payment; writing for oneself in study differs from paid writing for another. The daily excerpt closes after the haircut clause; the following study-and-preparation instruction belongs to the full classical gloss.

units.he: תא חזי כל אינון עמיקין סתימין דנפקי מגו מחשבה, וקלא נטיל לון, לא אתגליין עד דמלה מגלה לון, מאן מלה, היינו דבור, והאי דבור אקרי שבת, ובגין דשבת אקרי דבור, דבור דחול אסור בשבת, (וכך הוה עביד רבי שמעון, כד חמי לאמיה דהות משתעיא, הוה אמר לה אמא שתוקי שבת הוא ואסיר), בגין דדבור דא בעיא לשלטאה ולא אחרא, והאי דבור דאיהו אתי מסטרא דחשך, מגלה עמוקות מגויה, ומשמע מני חשך, ההוא דאתי מסטרא דחשך דכתיב מני דייקא.
units.en: Come and see: all those hidden depths that emerge from within thought, and that the voice carries, are not revealed until the word reveals them. What is “the word”? It is speech. This speech is called Shabbos; and because Shabbos is called speech, weekday speech is forbidden on Shabbos. (And this is what Rabbi Shimon would do: when he saw his mother speaking, he would say to her, “Mother, be silent; it is Shabbos, and [such speech] is forbidden.”) For this speech must rule, and not another. And this speech, which comes from the side of darkness, reveals depths from within it. The wording “from darkness” indicates that which comes from the side of darkness, for precisely “from” is written.
displayMeaningNotes: Thought, voice and revealing speech are distinguished. This speech is identified with Shabbos and contrasted with weekday speech. “[Such speech]” limits the instruction about silence to that contrast, not all speech on Shabbos.
The final exposition emphasizes מני, “from,” in מני חשך, “from darkness.” The report about Rabbi Shimon and his mother is parenthetical.

units.he:
אשרי אדם שמשים עצמו כשור לעול וכחמור למשאוי
ויושב וקורא ושונה בד״ת בכל יום תמיד וקורא
תורה נביאים וכתובים ושונה הלכות ומדרש וירבה בישיבה
וימעט בסחורה מיד רוח הקדש שורה עליו וכו׳ אמר אבא
אליהו ז״ל מעיד אני עלי שמים וארץ בין איש בין אשה בין
כותי בין ישראל בין עבד בין שפחה הכל לפי מעשיו של
אדם רוח הקדש שורה עליו . אשרי מי ששם כל אלו נגד
פניו בכל עת ויזכה להשלים בהם כל ימי חייו ולכלות עצמו
בהם כל ימי חייו ובכל מעשים האלו ובלבד שישמור עצמו
ולדבריו וגופו מכל חטא ועון זוכה לכל הכבוד הצפון לצדיקים
עד שאין מנין ושיעור ואין כל עין יכולה לראות ואין כל אוזן
יכולה לשמוע כבוד המתוקן לצדיקים ולחסידים וכן הוא אומר ומעולם לא שמעו ולא האזינו עין לא ראתה אלהים זולתך
יעשה למחכה לו :
units.en: Happy is the person who makes himself like an ox for the yoke and like a donkey for the burden, and sits, reads, and studies words of Torah every day continually: he reads Torah, Prophets, and Writings, studies laws and exposition, increases his time sitting in study, and diminishes his commerce. Immediately the Holy Spirit rests upon him, etc. Abba Elijah, of blessed memory, said: ‘I call heaven and earth to witness concerning me: whether man or woman, whether a Cuthean or an Israelite, whether a male slave or a female slave—everything is according to a person's deeds; the Holy Spirit rests upon him.’ Happy is the one who sets all these things before him at every moment and merits to complete all the days of his life with them, and to expend himself upon them all the days of his life. Through all these deeds, provided that he guards himself, his speech, and his body from every sin and iniquity, he merits all the honour stored up for the righteous, beyond number or measure. No eye can see, and no ear can hear, the honour prepared for the righteous and the pious. Thus it says: ‘From of old they have not heard, nor have they given ear; no eye has seen, O God, except You, [what] He will do for the one who waits for Him.’
displayMeaningNotes: ולדבריו is an unusual connective. The list is understood as guarding oneself, one’s speech and one’s body.

The closing quotation addresses God and explains that the righteous reward exceeds human sight and hearing. “[What]” links the unseen object to the following clause. “He will do” and “for Him” reflect the quotation’s third-person forms. Rashi on Isaiah 64:3 discusses both unseen reward and the plain-sense reading about no other god; here the paragraph uses the unseen-reward sense.
